They satisfy valence and momentum sum rules at the percent level and reproduce representative $pp\to\pi$ and $pp\to\gamma\pi$ cross sections within approximately 2% and 5%, respectively, in the kinematic regions studied. Compared with grid interpolation through LHAPDF, direct evaluation of the analytic expressions reduces the total Monte Carlo run time by about 11% and 30% in these two applications.

hep-ph.title: Has Quarkyonic Matter Been Seen in Lattice Simulations?
hep-ph.author: Kohei Fujikura, Kenji Fukushima, Yoshimasa Hidaka, Etsuko Itou, Larry McLerran
hep-ph.abstract: Quarkyonic Matter refers to the dual state of matter between confined hadrons and quasi-free quarks. This duality leads to a robust constraint on the behavior of the distribution functions. After a comprehensive review of Quarkyonic Matter based on the distribution functions, we discuss recent lattice data for two-color QCD in $(1+1)$ and $(3+1)$ dimensions at finite baryon number density and QCD in $(3+1)$ dimensions at finite isospin density, as well as the astrophysically inferred equation of state. Taken together, these results reveal a coherent picture consistent with the emergence of Quarkyonic Matter in lattice simulations. Future lattice calculations of baryon and gauge-invariant quark momentum distributions at high density would provide a more direct test of this interpretation.

hep-ph.title: Algorithmic Construction of Vector-Valued Modular Forms and Application to an $A_4\times\mathbb{Z}_4$-invariant Model of Leptons
hep-ph.author: Q. Bonnefoy, M. Rausch de Traubenberg, V. Saulquin
hep-ph.abstract: We present an algorithmic procedure that constructs the Vector-Valued Modular Forms (VVMFs) of finite modular groups, as well as its implementation in a companion code. The usual method consists in building the first few VVMFs, whose tensor products then generate the others. We address the difficulty of systematically finding the minimal set of VVMFs that suffices to produce all higher-weight ones, and we propose a method to identify it that makes use of the Burnside-Brauer theorem. For any given group, whose basic group-theoretic and representation-theoretic description is provided by the user, the code determines the minimal set of VVMFs, explicitly builds it using general results of the theory of such functions, then performs the tensor products that generate any other VVMF. Importantly, it automatically takes into account all caveats that might arise during the study of new groups. Our approach reproduces the known results for the finite modular groups explored in the recent phenomenological literature on modular flavor symmetries, and works for additional groups which we tested. We illustrate our algorithm and the working of our code by studying a model of leptons based on the unexplored finite modular group $A_4\times\mathbb{Z}_4$.

hep-ph.title: Top-Quark Pair Production and Decay in Extended Higgs Sectors
hep-ph.author: Andrea Banfi, Alexander Lind, Jonas M. Lindert, Vishakha Lingadahally
hep-ph.abstract: Extensions of the Higgs sector in the Standard Model address outstanding questions like the first-order electroweak phase transition and also present a rich collider phenomenology. The two-Higgs-doublet model is a minimal extension of the Standard Model with an extra complex $SU(2)_L$ doublet, and consists of an extra scalar, a pseudoscalar and a pair of charged Higgs bosons along with a Standard-Model-like Higgs boson. We present a modified version of the hvq library of the POWHEG-BOX-V2 event generator interfaced with the OpenLoops 2 amplitude generator to obtain predictions for top-quark pair production at NLO accuracy, including top-quark decays with full spin correlations in a framework that extends the SM Higgs sector with an extra heavy scalar and a pseudoscalar. The interference effects between the scalar and pseudoscalar signals, and the Standard Model QCD background are implemented. We include parton showers and hadronisation, and take detector effects into consideration. The status of our work and plans to extend it to future collider projects are discussed.

hep-ph.title: Signatures of Neutrinophilic Pion Dark Matter
hep-ph.author: Claire Chevallier, Ji-Heng Guo, Giacomo Landini
hep-ph.abstract: We study the phenomenology of pion dark matter coupled to neutrinos in a confining sector that dynamically generates both small neutrino masses and dark matter mass from gauge confinement. Dark matter semi-annihilation to active neutrinos or annihilation to light sterile neutrinos can reproduce the observed relic abundance through thermal freeze-out while satisfying constraints from self-interactions. In the first scenario, semi-annihilations of sub-GeV dark matter in the galactic halo produce a flux of antineutrinos which can provide a viable interpretation for the mild electron antineutrino excess reported by the Super-Kamiokande collaboration. We assess the potential of the JUNO detector to test this interpretation. In the second scenario, light sterile neutrinos can leave signatures through displaced vertex searches at accelerator facilities.

hep-ph.title: Testing the Spin of New Physics with Top Precision Measurements
hep-ph.author: André Lessa, Vinícius Rocca, Veronica Sanz
hep-ph.abstract: Precision measurements can reveal not only the presence of new physics, but also information about the dynamics that generated it. We study this question in top-pair production by comparing three top-philic scenarios: a colored scalar top partner, a colored vector-like fermion, and a spin-one $Z^\prime$ mediator. The first two contribute through loop corrections, while the $Z^\prime$ contributes at tree level. We show that the scalar and vector-like fermion scenarios match onto the same effective operator structure at low energies,making their distinction unfeasible using the EFT approach. However, near or above threshold their full loop amplitudes develop distinct momentum-dependent interference patterns. Using the top transverse momentum spectrum we find that resonant and loop-induced effects are relatively easy to distinguish, whereas separating the scalar and vector-like hypotheses is substantially more challenging. Nevertheless, their different analytic structures leave measurable information in the shape of the distribution. These results illustrate how precision differential measurements can probe the spin and dynamics of virtual new states even when they are not directly reconstructed, and motivate more powerful multidimensional analyses.

hep-ph.title: Joint Bayesian Inference for Extraction of Charmonium Long Distance Matrix Elements Using PYTHIA
hep-ph.author: Yubo Liu, Rongrong Ma
hep-ph.abstract: We present a joint Bayesian extraction of the nonrelativistic QCD long-distance matrix elements (LDMEs) for $J/\psi$, $\psi(2S)$, and $\chi_c$ production, using short-distance coefficients and feed-down structure implemented in PYTHIA 8.317. Rather than fitting each charmonium state separately, we construct channel-resolved responses that link parent production to daughter feed-down and infer all LDMEs simultaneously from 286 prompt charmonium measurements in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=5.02$-13 TeV at the LHC. The extracted LDMEs provide a good description of the data, with an overall $\chi^2/\mathrm{ndf}=1.18$. We also provide a positivity-constrained set that can be used directly as PYTHIA input. Using the extracted LDMEs, we predict prompt $J/\psi$ and $\psi(2S)$ cross sections at high transverse momentum in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=200$ GeV, which can be tested with RHIC data.

hep-ph.title: Novel hydrodynamic features in dissipative spin-polarized fluids
hep-ph.author: Zbigniew Drogosz, Wojciech Florkowski, Jakub Witkowski
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate an extension of perfect spin hydrodynamics that includes dissipation in the spin sector. The presence of dissipation implies that antisymmetric parts of the energy-momentum tensor should be taken into account. Their form follows from the Navier-Stokes or Israel-Stewart theory, which introduces a priori unknown kinetic coefficients and relaxation times. We find that the inclusion of the antisymmetric parts of the energy-momentum tensor has twofold effects: i) they form source terms for the spin tensor allowing for the transfer between the spin and orbital parts of the total angular momentum (spin-orbit interaction) and ii) they appear in the conservation laws for the energy and linear momentum, indirectly affecting the spin dynamics. Numerical results are obtained for two boost-invariant expansion geometries: one-dimensional longitudinal motion (Bjorken model) and two-dimensional boost-invariant and cylindrically symmetric expansion. They indicate (for various choices of the spin kinetic coefficients and the relaxation times) that the spin polarization tensor approaches thermal vorticity. We also observe that Israel-Stewart dynamics on the way to local equilibrium approaches first the Navier-Stokes regime. In general, we find that the Israel-Stewart formalism naturally helps to consistently combine the conservation laws for linear and angular momentum, while the Navier-Stokes framework itself can lead to a disruption in the structure of the equations through the inclusion of terms involving derivatives of an order higher than one.

hep-ph.title: Fermion$\text{-}$Monopole Scattering: A Unified Perspective
hep-ph.author: Hao Geng, Zekai Wang
hep-ph.abstract: We revisit the scattering of massless chiral fermions by a minimally charged BPS 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole. Existing proposals emphasize different aspects of this process and their connections are often unclear, giving rise to apparent conflicts concerning the outgoing states, energy conservation, and anomalous scattering amplitudes. We clarify the connection between different proposals within a common low-energy fermion-rotor description. Starting from the monopole background, we derive the rotor coupling and retain explicit fermion operators throughout the analysis. By adjoining a decoupled auxiliary scalar, we construct a dual theory that permits exact quantization. We show that the rotor vertex has a continuous spectral support down to zero energy and that its infrared exchange relations identify it as the twist dressing of the outgoing fermion. We also compute anomalous fermion correlators directly from fermion zero modes generated by winding configurations of the compact rotor. These results connect rotor dynamics, twisted outgoing states, and the zero-mode origin of anomalous correlators, resolving apparent conflicts and showing how the existing proposals fit into a mutually consistent picture within their common regime of applicability.

hep-ph.title: Constraining the spectral gap of 2d CFTs just above c=1
hep-ph.author: Nathan Benjamin, Kevin Langhoff, Wei Li, Jesse Thaler
hep-ph.abstract: We numerically study the space of compact unitary two-dimensional conformal field theories (2d CFTs) with central charge $c>1$ using the modular bootstrap. We focus on bounding the spectral gap $\Delta_{\rm gap}$ of such theories, namely the smallest scaling dimension among the non-vacuum primary operators. We use both a primal method that directly searches for consistent spectra and a dual method that yields rigorous exclusions. A key feature of our analysis is requiring the degeneracies of primary operators to be positive integers. At $c$ very near $1$, the integrality constraint greatly reduces the allowed spectral gap in both methods. For example, at $c-1 = 3\times 10^{-3}$ integrality strengthens the rigorous bound from $\Delta_{\rm gap} \lesssim 0.5$ to $\Delta_{\rm gap} < 0.041$. Our results suggest that the spectral gap might vanish as $c$ approaches $1$ from above.

hep-ph.title: Latest $ν$s from the Earliest Galaxies: Probing neutrino self-interactions with JWST
hep-ph.author: Ranjini Mondol, Priyank Parashari, Anirban Das, Vera Gluscevic, Ranjan Laha
hep-ph.abstract: Our Universe serves as a complementary laboratory for particle physics interactions. One intriguing possibility is that neutrinos may have beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) self-interactions, which can delay their free streaming and have an observable effect across different redshifts. Such interactions can induce scale-dependent changes in the matter power spectrum. The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has opened up a new window onto the early Universe by discovering a large population of high-redshift galaxies up to $z \sim 15$ and various probable galaxy candidates at even higher redshifts, between $z \sim 15-30$. Such high-redshift observations can probe the matter power spectrum on small scales, since structure formation is hierarchical and the structures hosting these high-redshift galaxies are therefore expected to be small. We, $\textit{for the first time}$, use the UV luminosity function data from JWST and combine them with the $\textit{Planck}$ CMB data to probe neutrino self-interactions ($\nu$SI). If only one neutrino flavor experiences such BSM interactions, then $\textit{Planck}$ + JWST data give a 95% C.L. upper limit on $\mathrm{Log}_{10}(G_{\mathrm{eff}}/\mathrm{MeV}^{-2})$ $\approx$ $-2.75$ and when all three flavors are interacting, the corresponding constraint becomes $\lesssim -3.41$; both stronger than those obtained using only $\textit{Planck}$ data. Our results highlight the power of this new observable, the high-redshift UV luminosity function from JWST as a complementary probe to terrestrial experiments, showing that small-scale observables can open a new window onto smaller neutrino self-interaction strengths.

hep-ph.title: Running Couplings in CP Violating Abelian Theories
hep-ph.author: Joshua Newey, John Terning, Christopher B. Verhaaren
hep-ph.abstract: We calculate the one- and two-loop running couplings for a massless photon coupled to dyons, including CP violating couplings. The electric and magnetic source vertices in the most general theory form a real coupling matrix $C$, while a current-current interaction depends on $C^T C$ and the quantized determinant $\det C$. These determine, respectively, the continuously running Coulombic interactions and the fixed antisymmetric Dirac--Schwinger--Zwanziger charge quantization condition which also determines pairwise helicity. The running preserves $\det C$, showing that the electric and magnetic couplings run inversely while every pairwise helicity remains constant. We comment on how the running of the CP-odd coupling $\theta$ relates to physical CP violation, which also depends on the spectrum, mass phases, and threshold corrections. We also show that an invertible field redefinition moves the CP-odd coupling between the current source terms and the photon kinetic terms; these are two descriptions of the same local interaction. Finally, we show that the result agrees with the Argyres--Douglas $\beta$ function ansatz.

hep-ph.title: Finite is not enough: Triviality bounds in nonlocal field theories
hep-ph.author: Fabian Wagner
hep-ph.abstract: An ultraviolet-finite theory need not be ultraviolet complete. This observation weakens the case for spacetime discreteness in quantum gravity if that case rests on removing ultraviolet divergences alone. We arrive at this observation by deriving the one-loop momentum-subtraction flow in four-dimensional $\phi^4$ theories with ultraviolet-suppressing form factors. The suppression freezes the running above the nonlocality scale, but the theory can hit a Landau pole before suppression sets in. We obtain a bound on the infrared coupling by requiring perturbative control at all scales. This bound varies only at the percent level across the examples we consider. We expect similar bounds in models of discrete spacetime. Thus, requiring ultraviolet completeness improves the predictivity of nonlocal theories.

hep-ph.title: Amplitude Analysis of the Invariant-Mass Spectra of Centrally Exclusively Produced $π^+π^-$ and $K^+K^-$ Pairs in $pp$ Collisions at $\sqrt{s}=510$ GeV
hep-ph.author: Aranya Giri, Barak Schmookler, Rene Bellwied
hep-ph.abstract: We present an amplitude analysis of the $\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ and $K^{+}K^{-}$ invariant-mass spectra from central exclusive $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=510~\mathrm{GeV}$, measured by the STAR experiment with forward-scattered protons tagged in the Roman Pot detectors. The $\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ channel is described with $f_{0}(500)$, $\rho^{0}(770)$, $f_{0}(980)$, $f_{2}(1270)$, $f_{0}(1500)$ and $f_{0}(1710)$ resonances with $\chi^{2}/\mathrm{ndf}=121.712/57$. The fit also yields $m_{f_{0}(980)}=0.989$ GeV and $\Gamma=0.091$ GeV. The $K^{+}K^{-}$ channel is described with $f_{0}(980)$, $f_{2}(1270)$, $f_{2}^{\prime}(1525)$ and $f_{0}(1710)$ resonances with $\chi^{2}/\mathrm{ndf}=14.662/15$. The fiducial cross sections for the individual resonances and interference terms were calculated, together with their ratios relative to the total fitted cross section. These ratios were compared across decay channels and qualitatively with previous measurements. A consistent flavor dependence of $f_{0}(1500)$ and $f_{0}(1710)$ has been derived for the highest RHIC collision energies, which is in agreement with low energy data.

hep-ph.title: Improved method for extracting low-energy expansion from OPE in mass-gapped theories
hep-ph.author: Hajime Furuta, Yukinari Sumino
hep-ph.abstract: Recently, Takaura proposed a new method for extracting the first nonzero coefficient of the low-energy expansion of an observable from its operator product expansion (OPE) in asymptotically free theories with a mass gap and a single threshold. The method uses a weight function to suppress the contribution of the ``duality-violation'' (DV) term that arises when relating the OPE to the low-energy expansion. We extend this method to low-energy expansion coefficients at arbitrary orders. We present two approaches: Method I uses weight functions that isolate the coefficients of low-energy expansion from the OPE. Method II subtracts the DV contribution from the OPE before the extraction. Applying these methods to the two-dimensional large-$N$ $O(N)$ nonlinear sigma model, we find that both methods successfully reconstruct higher-order low-energy expansion coefficients.

hep-ph.title: First broadband search for fixed-polarization dark photon dark matter with GigaBREAD
hep-ph.author: Jialin Yu, Stefan Knirck, Gabe Hoshino, Rakshya Khatiwada, Alex Lapuente, David W. Miller, Andrew Sonnenschein
hep-ph.abstract: We present the first search for fixed-polarization dark photon (DP) dark matter in the 44-52$\mu\mathrm{eV}$ mass range, corresponding to 10.7-12.5GHz. GigaBREAD is a room-temperature broadband dish antenna experiment in which DP convert to ordinary photons on a cylindrical metallic emission surface and are focused onto a radio-frequency receiver. Previous searches, including GigaBREAD and several other dish antenna searches, have assumed randomly polarized DP dark matter. However, vector dark matter produced by a misalignment-like mechanism may retain an approximately fixed polarization, leading to sidereal modulation of the detector response as the Earth rotates. We reanalyze the GigaBREAD data using a polarization-matched likelihood that accounts for the time-dependent projection of a fixed DP polarization onto the detector axis. We find no evidence for a fixed-polarization DP signal and set upper limits on the kinetic mixing parameter at the level of $\chi\sim10^{-12}$. These limits are about $20\%$ better than a naive limit obtained by rescaling the previous GigaBREAD limit under the fixed-polarization assumption.

hep-ph.title: Probing the Seed Effect of Supermassive Primordial Black Holes with Weak Gravitational Lensing
hep-ph.author: Lei Zu, Kazunori Kohri
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the cosmological implications of supermassive primordial black holes (PBHs) as a component of dark matter (DM), focusing on their seed effect on large-scale structure formation. In contrast to the Poisson effect associated with the discrete distribution of PBHs, the seed effect arises because PBHs act as early gravitational seeds, accreting surrounding DM and developing dense DM spikes to form dressed PBHs. These structures enhance the matter power spectrum, particularly on small scales. We model their contribution within the halo-model framework under two prescriptions for DM accretion: an optimistic scenario (Case 1) and a conservative scenario (Case 2), which predict different modifications to the 1-halo term. We constrain the PBH abundance using weak-lensing measurements from the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 (DES Y3), performing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis to derive upper limits on the PBH fraction $f_{\rm PBH}$, as a function of the PBH mass $M_{\rm PBH}$. We find that weak lensing places competitive constraints on supermassive PBHs, with the upper limits on $f_{\rm PBH}$ becoming progressively stronger toward higher PBH masses. Case 1, which predicts more efficient DM accretion and hence a larger enhancement of the matter power spectrum, yields stronger constraints than Case 2; in particular, it excludes $f_{\rm PBH}\gtrsim10^{-4}$ for $M_{\rm PBH}\gtrsim10^{10} M_\odot$. We further forecast the sensitivity of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) using mock weak-lensing data and find that the constraints could improve by approximately two orders of magnitude. Our results establish weak gravitational lensing as a sensitive probe of the seed effect of supermassive PBHs and demonstrate its potential to complement other cosmological and astrophysical searches.

hep-ph.title: Search for dark matter axions at 1-2 micro-eV with a RADES-DarkQuantum haloscope at CERN
hep-ph.author: Alberto Arcusa Puente, Sergio Arguedas Cuendis, Marcos Buetas Mata, Sergio Calatroni, Cristian Cogollos, Alejandro Díaz-Morcillo, Babette Döbrich, Jacob Egge, Elisa Gabbrielli, Javier Galindo Guarch, Jose María García-Barceló, Benito Gimeno, Yikun Gu, Sophia Hollick, Igor Garcia Irastorza, David Kittlinger, Adrian Lambies-Asensio, Axel Lindner, Manuel Meyer, Adrián Muñoz-Urán, Jose R. Navarro-Madrid, Tobias Ortmann, Sagar Paul, Angel Rodriguez, Kristof Schmieden, Laura Segui, Wolfgang Wernsdorfer, Mina Yami
hep-ph.abstract: The QCD axion remains one of the most compelling candidates for the dark matter of the Universe, yet the mass range around $1$\text{--}\SI{2}{\micro\electronvolt} remains essentially unexplored. In this paper, we describe a proposal to employ CERN's M1 superconducting magnet to deploy a haloscope to perform a search for galactic axion and axion-like particle dark matter providing continuous coverage from approximately 1.2 to 1.8 \SI{}{\micro\electronvolt}. Under conservative assumptions, the experiment can reach the QCD axion band over a significant fraction of the scanned range, while optimistic detector performance would allow sensitivity to benchmark models such as KSVZ and DFSZ over a large part of the explored mass interval. With the current long shut-down of CERN's accelerators providing a unique and timely window, such an experiment will deliver high-impact results even in conservative scenarios and potentially delivering a definitive test of the axion dark matter paradigm in the unexplored $1$\text{--}\SI{2}{\micro\electronvolt} mass range.

hep-ph.title: Quark-mass dependence of two-nucleon scattering
hep-ph.author: Jorge Baeza-Ballesteros, André Baião-Raposo, Davide Laudicina, Malcolm Lazarow, Thomas R. Richardson, Miguel Salg, John Bulava, Jeremy R. Green, Andrew Hanlon, Renwick J. Hudspith, Daniel Mohler, Colin Morningstar, Amy Nicholson, Fernando Romero-López, André Walker-Loud, Hartmut Wittig(for the Baryon Scattering Collaboration)
hep-ph.abstract: Understanding how the properties of the visible Universe depend on the parameters of the Standard Model of particle physics requires \emph{ab initio} theoretical computations. To that end, we investigate the quark-mass dependence of low-energy nucleon-nucleon scattering in the deuteron and dineutron channels. We perform lattice-QCD calculations at pion masses $M_\pi\approx 200$ and $280$ MeV and compare their results to phenomenology at the physical point and to a previous calculation at $M_\pi\approx 710$ MeV. Scattering amplitudes, phase shifts, and threshold parameters are determined from finite-volume spectra using quantization conditions that explicitly incorporate long-distance effects from one-pion exchange. We analyze the pion-mass dependence of scattering lengths and effective ranges using chiral effective field theory with Weinberg and Kaplan-Savage-Wise power countings. From this, we estimate the pion-mass derivatives of the inverse scattering lengths and binding momentum, at the physical point. Both power countings indicate that the deuteron unbinds near $M_\pi\approx 220$ MeV.

hep-ph.title: The Mass Gap Approach to QCD. III. Solution of the gluon confinement problem
hep-ph.author: Vakhtang Gogokhia, Gergely Gábor Barnaföldi
hep-ph.abstract: We present reports on progress in the solution of the gluon confinement problem and in the explanation of the scale breaking in the asymptotic freedom regime in QCD. It is based on the previously formulated the mass gap approach to QCD, which sheds the light on a mass origin in its ground state. We have established the exact expression for the full gluon propagator. One of its solution allows to sum up all the severe (more singular than $1/q^2$) infrared singularities which can be accommodated by a single full gluon propagator. In order to correctly treat them, we have developed a formalism of the joint use of the theory of functions of complex variable, and the dimensional regularization method correctly implemented into the theory of distributions. Despite the presence of the mass gap, gluons remain massless. Our solution satisfies the two boundary conditions: it dominates over all other possible solutions at large distances but itself prevents gluons to appear in the physical spectrum. It possesses the asymptotic freedom behaviour at short distances. We discuss the connection of our results to the Elitzur's theorem.

hep-ph.title: Can $n_s$ hint at a parity-odd sector of gravity?
hep-ph.author: Christian Dioguardi
hep-ph.abstract: We study slow-roll inflation in the context of metric-affine gravity. We consider the most general projectively invariant metric-affine theory at most quadratic in the distortion and linear in curvature with no propagating torsion and non-metricity and couple it non-minimally to a scalar field. We focus on the class of $\xi$-attractors, in which a single function $f(\phi)$ fixes the whole scalar sector. Integrating out the non-dynamical distortion generates a correction to the kinetic term $k(\phi)$ which is $f'(\phi)^2$ times a ratio of polynomials in $f(\phi)$. The new kinetic term can develop poles at finite field values, where the distortion field equations degenerate. We classify the poles and derive the conditions on the effective couplings for poles of order $p=2$ and $p=3$, the maximal order allowed in this setting. We then proceed to study inflation. Second-order poles realize $\alpha$-attractors with $\alpha$ fixed by the residue and are already available in the parity-even sector of the theory. Third-order poles instead require the parity-odd sector: whenever the parity-odd quadratic couplings vanish, the kinetic function splits into two independent terms with poles of order at most $p=2$. Third-order pole-inflation, as we confirm numerically for $f(\phi)\propto\phi^2$, yields $r\propto N_*^{-3/2}$ with a tunable amplitude and $n_s\simeq 1-\tfrac{3}{2N_*}$, a spectral index mildly larger than the $\alpha$-attractor prediction and well centered in the region preferred by the current combination of ACT, SPT and DESI data. Moreover, when inflation happens far away from the pole we also find a further universal attractor, an inverse-linear plateau, with $n_s \simeq 1-\frac{4}{3N_*}$ and $r\propto N_*^{-4/3}$, testable with the forthcoming BICEP/Keck observations.

hep-ph.title: Quantum transport of vortex electrons in bending magnets and circular accelerators
hep-ph.author: D. Karlovets, I. Pavlov, A. Murtazin, D. Grosman, X. Chen
hep-ph.abstract: Controlling the sizes and phase structure of single-particle wave packets in accelerators remains an experimental challenge and requires understanding how bending magnets transform these states. An important example is transporting relativistic vortex electrons through the magnets to a collision point while keeping a narrow orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) distribution. We derive an effective Hamiltonian that accounts for the packet acceleration, employ it to obtain a generalized BMT-like equation, match the electron state at both magnet boundaries, and calculate the mean OAM and its variance. A half turn can reverse the mean OAM relative to the momentum while broadening its distribution, so recovering the mean does not ensure state recovery. We identify windows in packet sizes and bend angles for a small OAM spread and show that weak bends can produce narrow distributions with the mean OAM tilted relative to the momentum, making these states candidates for spatiotemporal vortices. For a few MeV electrons, we propose to use half-turn magnets that leave the mean OAM nearly antiparallel to the momentum while keeping its distribution narrow. For a circular orbit in a uniform field, the OAM variance after the exit grows as $N^2$ over $N$ turns, favoring linear accelerators, such as LINAC at JINR, for first experiments in MeV range.

hep-ph.title: Manifestation of scale symmetry in nuclear medium
hep-ph.author: Yong-Liang Ma
hep-ph.abstract: This memorial tribute to Mannque Rho focuses on the role of scale symmetry in baryonic matter, especially on its profound influence on the possible resolution of the ``quenched $g_A$" problem in the Gamow-Teller transition of nuclei, the pseudoconformal structure of dense nuclear matter and the origin of the peak of sound velocity of nuclear matter. The discussion is based on the genuine dilaton scenario, anchored on the Crewther-Tunstall infrared fixed point, which provides a unified framework where scale symmetry---broken explicitly by the QCD trace anomaly---can be spontaneously broken, yielding the scalar $f_0(500)$ as a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson. In nuclear medium, this scenario serves as a natural foundation of the Brown-Rho scaling---a relation that has been central to nuclear physics for over three decades. The sound velocity of nuclear matter exhibits a characteristic peak at intermediate densities arising from the kink behavior of the dilaton field, a unique signature of scale symmetry realization that distinguishes the dilaton-compensated effective theory from conventional Walecka-type models. At higher densities, the approach to the dilaton-limit fixed point produces pseudo-conformal behavior with sound velocity $v_s^2 = 1/3$ saturating from below at $n \gtrsim 3n_0$, while the trace of the energy-momentum tensor remains nonzero. The framework also provides a natural resolution of the long-standing ``quenched $g_A$" problem, demonstrating that nuclear correlations, not fundamental quenching, account for the effective axial coupling approaching unity. The continuity from the unitary limit at low density to the dilaton limit at high density suggests a pervasive role for scale symmetry in nuclear dynamics across all density regimes.

hep-ph.title: Linking chiral nuclear forces to light-ion collisions: a global sensitivity analysis
hep-ph.author: Thomas Duguet, Andreas Ekström, Giuliano Giacalone, Gaute Hagen, Takayuki Miyagi, Alexander Tichai
hep-ph.abstract: Ultrarelativistic $^{16}$O+$^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne+$^{20}$Ne collisions recently performed at the Large Hadron Collider have imaged quadrupole and octupole correlations between nucleons through the collective flow of emitted hadrons. We establish a quantitative link between these correlations and the low-energy constants (LECs) that enter chiral inter-nucleon interactions. Emulators built using the subspace-projected coupled-cluster method enable a global sensitivity analysis of the ground-state quadrupole mean-square eccentricity, revealing that quadrupole correlations respond linearly and additively to all 16 LECs at next-to-next-to-leading order in the chiral expansion. The sensitivities differ markedly in $^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne, and are complementary to those of the binding energy and charge radius, the bulk observables to which nuclear interactions are typically calibrated. In particular, $^{20}$Ne collisions dominantly probe the spin-orbit part of two-nucleon interactions. Soft-particle correlations in light-ion collisions thus constitute a new type of data to study nuclear forces and their emergence from quantum chromodynamics.

hep-ph.title: Hypersurface covariance in relativistic local equilibrium
hep-ph.author: You-yu Li, Shuai Y.F. Liu
hep-ph.abstract: Defining equilibrium typically requires specifying a three-dimensional spacelike hypersurface. While global equilibrium is hypersurface covariant, calculations involving local equilibrium can exhibit hypersurface dependence. In this work, we use polarization in heavy-ion collisions within the Zubarev response approach as an example to show that the hypersurface dependence arising from the local-equilibrium part of the density operator is canceled by an overlooked nondissipative contribution from its so-called ``dissipative part". We establish a hypersurface-covariant Zubarev framework for general geometries by consistently including both nondissipative and dissipative parts, eliminating dependence on the arbitrary hypersurface vector. The remaining frame dependence is physical: it arises from the medium rest frame entering the particle distribution and the time direction of the dissipative process, which usually coincide. This resolves, in principle, the longstanding and widely discussed conceptual disagreement over hypersurface dependence between two influential studies addressing the sign puzzles of $\Lambda$-hyperon polarization in heavy-ion collisions

hep-ph.title: Novel collider signatures in the type-I 2HDM+$a$ model
hep-ph.author: Spyros Argyropoulos, Ulrich Haisch, Ilia Kalaitzidou
hep-ph.abstract: The 2HDM+$a$ model is one of the main models used in the interpretations of dark matter searches at the LHC. So far, all the 2HDM+$a$ benchmarks considered by the ATLAS and CMS experiments are limited to a type-II Yukawa sector, in which the Higgs bosons $A$, $H$, and $H^\pm$ are all constrained to be mass-degenerate and heavier than around $600 \, {\rm GeV}$. In this work, we present the first detailed study of 2HDM+$a$ models with a type-I Yukawa sector, which, for moderate values of $\tan\beta$, lift the constraints from flavour physics, allowing the extra Higgs bosons to be even lighter than the $125 \, {\rm GeV}$ Higgs boson discovered at the LHC. We discuss several benchmarks where the $A$, $H$, and $H^\pm$ states are not necessarily mass-degenerate and the signatures that arise in these models, some of which have not yet been explored at the LHC. We present the dominant channels in the studied benchmarks and the expected sensitivity in Run 2 data using truth-level analyses and discuss potential improvements in the experimental searches for Run 3.

hep-ph.title: Lorentz-Equivariance without Limitations
hep-ph.author: Luigi Favaro, Gerrit Gerhartz, Fred A. Hamprecht, Peter Lippmann, Sebastian Pitz, Tilman Plehn, Huilin Qu, Jonas Spinner
hep-ph.abstract: Lorentz Local Canonicalization (LLoCa) ensures exact Lorentz-equivariance for arbitrary neural networks with minimal computational overhead. For the LHC, it equivariantly predicts local reference frames for each particle and propagates any-order tensorial information between them. We apply it to graph networks and transformers. We showcase its cutting-edge performance on amplitude regression, end-to-end event generation, and jet tagging. For jet tagging, we introduce a large top tagging dataset to benchmark LLoCa versions of a range of established benchmark architectures and highlight the importance of symmetry breaking.

hep-ph.title: Higgs-Portal Stueckelberg Dark Matter
hep-ph.author: Antonio De Felice, Takehiro Ogura, Shinji Tsujikawa, Kimiko Yamashita
hep-ph.abstract: We study dark photon dark matter X associated with a dark $U(1)_X$ gauge symmetry. To evade laboratory and cosmological constraints on kinetic mixing with the Standard Model $U(1)_Y$, we assign a $Z_2$-odd dark parity to X that forbids such mixing. The leading interactions then arise from gauge-invariant dimension-6 Higgs-portal operators, including both parity-even and parity-odd terms. We assume that the dark matter mass is generated via the Stueckelberg mechanism. In the interacting Stueckelberg EFT, a gauge-invariant dimension-6 parent reduces in unitary gauge to the nominal dimension-4 Higgs-portal interaction $(H^†H)X_\mu X^\mu$, with its coefficient correlated with $m_X^2/\Lambda^2$, while additional derivative operators are organized by the same longitudinal-mode power counting. We investigate freeze-in production of X from Higgs-pair annihilations after reheating, incorporating both field-strength and Stueckelberg-allowed operators. First, we consider the case in which the Wilson coefficients of the gauge-invariant dimension-6 operators, C and $\tilde C$, are of order unity. Under a conservative single-cutoff power counting in which the strong-coupling scales of the longitudinal mode lie above the cutoff of the field-strength effective theory, we find that the Stueckelberg contributions remain subdominant in dark matter production. We emphasize that this ordering of scales is an explicit assumption rather than a universal consequence of perturbative unitarity. Next, we explore a more general situation in which C and $\tilde C$ are smaller than unity. In this second case, Stueckelberg-allowed operators can become comparable and generate contributions proportional to $T_{reh}^3$, $T_{reh}^5$, and $T_{reh}^7$, including sign-dependent interference effects. For both cases, we show that there exists a wide parameter space consistent with the observed dark matter relic density.

hep-ph.title: Baryogenesis and EDMs in the 2HDM with a Complex Singlet
hep-ph.author: Björn Garbrecht, Edward Wang
hep-ph.abstract: We perform the first joint analysis of baryogenesis from initial Higgs charges (also called Higgsogenesis) and electric dipole moments (EDMs) in a model with two Higgs doublets, a complex scalar, and a Majorana fermion. In our proposed scenario, baryogenesis happens in three steps: (1) The decay of the scalar produces an asymmetry between the two Higgs doublets which is partly transferred to fermions via Standard Model processes. (2) This asymmetry is converted into a $B-L$ charge via interactions mediated by the Majorana fermion. (3) The weak sphaleron processes partially convert the resulting $B-L$ charge into a $B$ asymmetry. We perform a numerical analysis of baryogenesis and the EDM contributions and find that, due to resonant enhancement, baryogenesis is possible with singlet masses as low as $10^5$ GeV. We also find that for some parameters, the model can give large contributions to the electron and neutron EDM while also producing baryogenesis. The present scenario offers a new perspective on interpreting observational bounds in terms of cosmology: Because it relies on out-of-equilibrium decays, the questions of baryogenesis and $CP$ violation in the Higgs sector may be linked with EDM signals without the additional assumption of a first order electroweak phase transition.

hep-ph.title: Hadronic tau decays at higher orders in QCD
hep-ph.author: Gauhar Abbas, Debabina Biswas, Pratham Dadhich, Vartika Singh
hep-ph.abstract: We ask what the four known coefficients of the Adler function in massless QCD can support about the unknown coefficient $c_{5,1}$ of $a^5$. In fixed-order perturbation theory the Adler-to-moment map is triangular with unit diagonal; hence a multi-weight relative test of a common forecast reduces exactly to one absolute coefficient tolerance. For three complementary weights, a ten-percent withheld-order test requires $|\widehat c_{4,1}-c_{4,1}|\leq2.1509$ and resolves $c_{5,1}$ only to about $\pm24$. Direct Shanks/Padé continuation cannot reach the usual literature range without reversing the sign of its next defect. We therefore apply a cross-validated renormalon-closure (CVRC) protocol to a pure-power Beneke--Jamin-type Borel ansatz. CVRC calibrates and tests this declared structure; it is not a new renormalon model. The calibrated construction gives the conditional estimate $c_{5,1}=248\pm30\,(\mathrm{struct})\pm74\,(\mathrm{method})=248\pm80$. The band is nonstatistical, and a recursive test misses the known $c_{4,1}$ by $29.9\%$. Thus the result is a model-qualified estimate consistent with existing determinations, not evidence that four coefficients determine the fifth.

hep-ph.title: Scaling laws for amplitude surrogates
hep-ph.author: Henning Bahl, Victor Bresó-Pla, Anja Butter, Joaquín Iturriza Ramirez
hep-ph.abstract: Scaling laws describing the dependence of neural network performance on the amount of training data, the spent compute, and the network size have emerged across a huge variety of machine learning task and datasets. In this work, we systematically investigate these scaling laws in the context of amplitude surrogates for particle physics. We show that the scaling coefficients are connected to the number of external particles of the process. Our results demonstrate that scaling laws are a useful tool to achieve desired precision targets.

hep-ph.title: Mixed Freeze-In and Freeze-Out Histories and Dark-Sector Decays in a $\mathbb{Z}_4$ Two-Scalar Model
hep-ph.author: J. P. Carvalho-Corrêa, B. A. Couto e Silva, B. L. Sánchez-Vega
hep-ph.abstract: We study dark matter production in a renormalisable $\mathbb{Z}_4$ Higgs-portal model containing a complex scalar $S_A$ and a real scalar $S_B$, where one or both states remain out of thermal equilibrium with the Standard Model bath. We follow their coupled evolution through conversion, semi-annihilation, and the decay $S_B\to S_A S_A$ when kinematically allowed. We impose theoretical consistency conditions, limits on invisible Higgs decays, and LZ direct-detection bounds, accounting for each component's relic fraction. We check WIMP/FIMP assignments against interaction rates. When both states are stable, we find viable FIMP--FIMP and mixed WIMP--FIMP scenarios. In mixed cases, the WIMP-like state remains constrained by its Higgs-portal interactions, with the surviving points mainly concentrated near the Higgs resonance. The FIMP-like state can, however, provide a substantial fraction of the relic density with a negligible direct-detection signal. For $M_{S_B}>2M_{S_A}$, the decay of the heavier scalar leads to three production histories: SuperWIMP production, injection-assisted freeze-out, and sequential freeze-in. The mechanism depends on parent and daughter production. These decays can increase the abundance of a WIMP after freeze-out or contribute to the final abundance of a FIMP, changing the relation between the daughter's Higgs coupling and its relic density. Since the primary decays produce no Standard Model particles, electromagnetic and hadronic BBN bounds on visible decay products do not apply directly. We find $r_{\rm BBN}\ll1$ throughout the retained sample. To assess effects on structure formation, we use the dark matter fraction produced through decays and an equivalent thermal-WDM mass as approximate diagnostics. Some late-decay configurations are flagged as potentially warm, whereas the sequential freeze-in sample satisfies $m_{\rm WDM}^{\rm eq}\gtrsim1~\mathrm{MeV}$.

hep-ph.title: Analysis of the $D_0^*(2300)$ resonance from lattice QCD under chiral symmetry
hep-ph.author: Jing Luo, Bing Wu, Pan-Pan Shi, Meng-Lin Du
hep-ph.abstract: We reanalyze the lattice spectra for $I=1/2$ $D\pi$ scattering in the $A_1^+$ irreducible representation from [Phys. Rev. D 111, 014503 (2025)] to investigate the impact of chiral and SU(3) flavor symmetries in $S$-wave $D\pi$ scattering and the $D_0^*(2300)$ resonance. By fitting the phase shifts obtained via Lüscher's formula with both traditional and chirally modified effective-range expansion and $K$-matrix parameterizations, we find that the chiral factor shifts the extracted pole mass closer to the threshold (especially for resonances) and substantially reduces the resonance width. These findings are confirmed by unitarized chiral perturbation theory through a direct fit to the lattice spectra with both the single-channel and the $D\pi$-$D\eta$-$D_s\bar{K}$ coupled-channel schemes. Once the coupled channels are incorporated, the two-pole structure of the $D_0^*(2300)$ emerges. The trajectories of the two poles are investigated by varying the pion mass.

hep-ph.title: Ultra-High-Energy Tau Neutrinos as Probes of Lorentz Invariance
hep-ph.author: Vedran Brdar, Samiur R. Mir
hep-ph.abstract: Neutrino telescopes have detected astrophysical neutrinos with energies up to ${O}(100)$ PeV. Several current and proposed experiments aim to observe neutrinos at even higher energies, with the goal of detecting cosmogenic neutrinos. This increase in neutrino energy makes tests of Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) particularly appealing, since the effects of higher-dimension LIV operators on neutrino propagation grow rapidly with energy. In this work, we investigate the potential of the upcoming experiments GRAND and POEMMA to probe LIV in the neutrino sector through the detection of ultra-high-energy tau neutrinos. We generate the cosmogenic neutrino flux using SimProp and interface it with a calculation of neutrino flavor transition probabilities in the presence of LIV effects. Deviations from standard flavor transition probabilities manifest as changes in the expected tau neutrino event rates at GRAND and POEMMA. We first consider the case with a single nonzero LIV operator of various dimensions, and find that the projected sensitivities exceed existing limits from lower-energy probes by orders of magnitude. We then explore scenarios with multiple nonzero LIV parameters and show that their interplay can significantly modify the sensitivities compared to the single-parameter case. Overall, we find that upcoming observations of ultra-high-energy tau neutrinos will place some of the most stringent constraints on LIV.

hep-ph.title: Dilaton-Induced Resonant Production of Ultralight Vector Dark Matter
hep-ph.author: Imtiaz Khan, G. Mustafa, Jehanzad Zafar, Farruh Atamurotov, Ahmadjon Abdujabbarov, Chengxun Yuan
hep-ph.abstract: We consider the production of ultralight vector dark matter through a dilatonic half-mass resonance in the presence of an oscillating spectator scalar. The cosmological condition is that the Floquet instability becomes efficient before the spectator contributes dominantly to the expansion. We express this condition in terms of the microscopic modulation parameter $\epsilon_i=\Phi_i/M$ and the gravitational onset fraction $r_i=\Phi_i^2/(6\Mpl^2)$. For a background with constant equation-of-state parameter $w_b$, the narrow-band result gives $\mu/H\propto a^{3w_b/2}$; the ratio therefore grows as $a^{1/2}$ during radiation domination and remains constant for matter-like expansion. Requiring delayed amplification to precede spectator domination gives the amplitude-independent bound $M/\Mpl\lesssim\sqrt6\,c_1\simeq0.31$, with $c_1\simeq1/8$ for the linear half-mass branch. An expanding-background calculation gives $a_\star<a_{\rm dom}$ for sub-Planckian $M$, whereas $M\simeq\Mpl$ delays efficient growth until after domination. Using the efficient-transfer normalization, we obtain $m_{\gamma'}\propto r_i^{-2}$, so that $m_{\gamma'}\sim10^{-20}$--$10^{-18}\,{\rm eV}$ corresponds to $r_i\sim10^{-5}$--$10^{-4}$ rather than to early spectator domination. The canonical polarization analysis shows a more infrared-localized longitudinal spectrum than the transverse spectrum, while derivative terms associated with canonical normalization change the leading Floquet exponents at order unity. Stückelberg and Higgsed realizations lead to different ultraviolet consistency conditions, including radial-mode decoupling and symmetry-restoration bounds. These conditions select a radiation-era, perturbative, infrared-dominated regime with a sub-Planckian kinetic scale for production.

hep-ph.title: Parton Distribution Functions from Large Momentum Expansion of Current-Current Correlators
hep-ph.author: Jialu Zhang, Xiangdong Ji, Andreas Schäfer, Rui Zhang, Christian Zimmermann
hep-ph.abstract: The universality of the large momentum expansion allows computing parton distribution functions (PDFs) starting from any Euclidean correlator with appropriate large momentum Fourier Components. Here we consider current-current correlators which have been used in short-distance expansion to obtain moments of PDFs. The advantage of such correlators is that they have simple renormalization properties and do not have linear power divergences as in quasi-PDF. However, in lattice calculations, four-point functions are needed. Here we present an expansion formula with current-current correlators up to the next-to-leading order, and preliminary numerical calculations with four-point functions.

hep-ph.title: Freeze-in $SU(2)$ vector dark matter at low reheating temperature
hep-ph.author: Dilip Kumar Ghosh, Sourav Gope, Xiao-Gang He, Xuan Hong, Sk Jeesun
hep-ph.abstract: The freeze-in mechanism for dark matter (DM) requires extremely feeble interactions with the Standard Model (SM), preventing thermal equilibrium in the early Universe and typically evading experimental detection. However, for sufficiently low reheating temperatures ($T_{\rm RH}$), the observed relic abundance can be realized with larger couplings, opening prospects for experimental searches. In this work, we investigate freeze-in production of $SU(2)_{\rm HS}$ vector dark matter (VDM) in a low-$T_{\rm RH}$ cosmology. The framework naturally contains three mass-degenerate stable VDM candidates without the need for any additional discrete symmetry. We perform a systematic study of the dark matter phenomenology and identify the parameter space consistent with the observed relic abundance. We work with the approximation of instantaneous reheating and consider the DM abundance to be negligible at $T_{\rm RH}$. In contrast to conventional freeze-in scenarios, the required DM couplings can be sizable, rendering part of the parameter space already constrained by existing direct searches like PandaX-4T and LZ, while a significant region remains within the reach of future experiments such as DARWIN. Though one can realize the freeze-in mechanism for an abelian $U(1)_X$ vector DM models as well, we find that the non-abelian structure of the $SU(2)_{\rm HS}$ scenario leads to a distinct feature due to a larger number of dark matter particles, resulting in an enlarged viable parameter space due to the multiplicity of dark matter states.

hep-ph.title: Defining a Minimum Resolution for Unbinned Analyses
hep-ph.author: Manuel Szewc
hep-ph.abstract: Collider analyses combine rigorous statistical techniques with state-of-the-art Machine Learning models. However, when the latter are used directly to estimate the likelihood function of the background, hard to quantify systematic effects may bias the estimation of the relevant signal parameters. To address this problem, we present the Minimum Resolution Likelihood (MRL) method, which defines a Fiducial Signal Region that aims to turn systematic effects into statistical uncertainties. We show with examples that the resulting signal strength estimation has a reduced bias, with the effect depending on the sample size and type of signal considered. We consider both toy examples and a realistic application based on the HI-SIGMA technique applied to di-Higgs searches.

hep-ph.title: Revisiting $\bar B^0 \rightarrow Λ_c^+ \bar p$ decay with higher twist corrections
hep-ph.author: Zhi-Tian Zou, Ying Li, Zhou Rui
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the single-charmed baryonic decays $\bar B^0 \to \Lambda_c^+ \bar p$ and $\bar B^0 \to \bar\Lambda_c^- p$, which receive contributions from both $W$-emission and $W$-exchange topologies, within the framework of perturbative QCD (PQCD). Higher-power corrections associated with the hadronic light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of both the initial- and final-state hadrons are systematically taken into account. We find that these higher-twist contributions play an important role in baryonic $B$ decays and cannot be neglected. A sizable destructive interference between the $W$-emission and $W$-exchange amplitudes is observed, which significantly reduces the predicted branching fraction of $\bar B^0 \to \Lambda_c^+ \bar p$ and leads to improved agreement with experimental measurements. The doubly Cabibbo-suppressed decay $\bar B^0 \to \bar\Lambda_c^- p$ is studied for the first time. Its branching fraction is predicted to be of order $10^{-8}$, placing it within the reach of future high-luminosity experiments. We further present the first theoretical predictions for the decay asymmetry parameters of both channels, which provide additional observables for testing the underlying decay dynamics and can be confronted with future experimental data.

hep-ph.title: Radiative decays of $X(3872)$ within $D{\bar D}^*$ molecular framework
hep-ph.author: Hao-Dong Cai, Run-Hao Chen, Yuan-Jun Gao, Zhao-Sai Jia, Gang Li, Shi-Dong Liu
hep-ph.abstract: Within the framework of nonrelativistic effective field theory, we calculate the radiative decay widths of the process $X(3872) \to D\bar{D} \gamma$ while taking into account the $D\bar{D}$ final-state interactions via resonance saturation. The $X(3872)$ is treated as a $D^*\bar{D} +\rm c.c.$ bound state with $J^{PC}=1^{++}$. For a representative mixing angle $\theta=\pi/4$, our numerical calculations predict that the tree-level partial decay width for $X(3872) \to D^0 \bar{D}^0\gamma$ can reach approximately $7.3$ keV, while that for $X(3872) \to D^+ D^- \gamma$ is less than $1$ keV. It is found that the contribution of the triangle loop diagrams to the total decay width of $X(3872) \to D^0 \bar{D}^0\gamma$ is very small, amounting to less than $1\%$ of the tree-level result. For the $X(3872)\to D^+ D^-\gamma $ decay, the contribution from the triangle loop diagrams is relatively more significant, enhancing the total decay width by roughly $1.3\%$ relative to the tree-level result. We expect that the present predictions based on the molecular picture of the $X(3872)$ can be tested by future experiments.

hep-ph.title: Leptogenesis with sub-electroweak-scale reheating temperature
hep-ph.author: Basabendu Barman, Arindam Basu, Debasish Borah, Nayan Das
hep-ph.abstract: We study the generation of the baryon asymmetry of the Universe via leptogenesis during the post-inflationary reheating epoch, considering reheating temperatures below the temperature of sphaleron freeze-out. Within the framework of a monomial inflaton potential during reheating, we analyze three perturbative reheating scenarios in which the inflaton decays into (i) a pair of Standard Model (SM)-like bosons, (ii) a pair of SM-like fermions, or (iii) exclusively into a pair of heavy right-handed neutrinos, which eventually decays into the SM final states after briefly dominating the energy density of the Universe. For each case, we identify the regions of parameter space that successfully reproduce the observed baryon asymmetry consistently tracking the sphaleron interaction rate during reheating, while satisfying existing cosmological constraints. We also highlight the potential of future primordial gravitational wave observations to probe this class of scenarios.

hep-ph.title: Model analysis on the effectiveness of the HAL QCD method for hadron-hadron interactions
hep-ph.author: Takayasu Sekihara(1), Kei Fujiwara(1) ((1) Kyoto Prefectural U.)
hep-ph.abstract: The HAL QCD method has been one of the powerful tools to extract hadron-hadron interactions directly from lattice QCD simulation data. In this paper, we aim at examining the effectiveness of the HAL QCD method by deriving a formula to calculate quantities in the HAL QCD method, such as the so-called R-correlators and HAL QCD local potentials, from the hadron-hadron scattering amplitudes within effective models. In this framework, we can judge whether the HAL QCD local potential, evaluated in the present formula, reproduces the properties of the original hadron-hadron interaction or not via the scattering amplitude, which is a solution of the Lippmann--Schwinger equation with the original hadron-hadron interaction as an input. In an analysis within a simple model of elastic scattering, we show that, when the original interaction is predominantly local, the HAL QCD local potentials quantitatively reproduce phase shifts of the hadron-hadron scatterings and correctly indicate the existence/absence of the bound state with its binding energy $\sim$ MeV. Higher-order corrections in the derivative expansion of the HAL QCD nonlocal potentials can provide a better description of the binding energies of the bound states. The lattice discretization and finite-volume effects of spacetime modify the results only slightly, as long as their scale is not comparable to the interaction range. Furthermore, we consider the $\bar{K} N$ potential in a bare to $\bar{K} N$ transition amplitude, which shows singular behavior around the origin in the recent HAL QCD results of the lattice QCD simulation data, and discuss the cause of such singular behavior in the HAL QCD method through our model analysis of the $\bar{K} N$ scattering.

hep-ph.title: Quarkoniumlike states above open-flavor thresholds in Born-Oppenheimer EFT
hep-ph.author: Nora Brambilla, Roberto Bruschini, Abhishek Mohapatra, Fang-Zheng Peng, Tommaso Scirpa
hep-ph.abstract: Many quarkoniumlike states have been observed above open-flavor thresholds, but their organization and internal structure remain unsettled. We study the isoscalar hidden-charm and hidden-bottom sectors in Born--Oppenheimer effective field theory (BOEFT), between the spin--isospin averaged $S+S$ and $S+P$ thresholds. At leading order, heavy-quark spin decouples, and the quarkonium static potential mixes through string breaking with the lowest tetraquark/open-flavor BO potentials of the same quantum numbers. These potentials are constrained by QCD symmetries, their short- and long-distance behavior, and lattice-QCD data. The only calibrated parameter is the lowest $1^{--}$ adjoint meson mass, fixed from the shallow multiplet associated with the $\chi_{c1}(3872)$. Using $T$-matrix, $K$-matrix, and complex-scaling methods, we determine bound states and resonance poles, their masses, pole widths from the included nonstrange $S+S$ channels, normalized pole couplings, and prescription-dependent quarkonium--open-flavor composition measures. The spectrum exhibits a common heavy-quark-spin-symmetry multiplet organization. Most poles are short-distance, predominantly quarkonium resonances. The same equations generate shallow, spatially extended, open-flavor-dominated states with molecular long-distance characteristics. Their binding energies, radii, and small quarkonium components are highly sensitive to the adjoint meson mass, whereas the higher spectrum is more stable. The equations also predict a more compact open-flavor-dominated resonance in the $l = 0$ bottomoniumlike sector, with a dominant $P$-wave open-flavor component. Together with the hybrid levels, the spectrum provides multiplet assignments for most candidates. States not naturally accommodated point to the need for hidden-strange and $S+P$ tetraquark/open-flavor BO sectors and for hybrid--tetraquark and hybrid--quarkonium mixings.

hep-ph.title: Spontaneous Scoto-leptogenesis
hep-ph.author: Arghyajit Datta, Hyun Min Lee, Jun-Ho Song
hep-ph.abstract: We propose a low-scale spontaneous leptogenesis scenario within the dynamical minimal scotogenic model for accommodating neutrino masses and inert scalar dark matter simultaneously. Thus, we dub the mechanism Spontaneous Scoto-leptogenesis. In this setup, a rolling Majoron arising from the global $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry breaking induces an effective chemical potential for the $B-L$ charge in the presence of $B-L$ violating interactions that allow for the efficient decays and inverse decays of right handed neutrinos (RHN) and RHN mediated scattering, so it gives rise to the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe through the electroweak sphaleron conversion. The mechanism becomes effective in the strong washout regime and successfully lowers the viable mass scale of the lightest RHN to the range of TeV scales, thereby making the thermal scotogenic leptogenesis with two hierarchical RHNs accessible to direct tests. We identify the roles of the $\lambda_5$ coupling for spontaneous leptogenesis and inert scalar dark matter through the efficient erasure of the inert scalar asymmetry. We also explore the regime for Majoron dark matter from the kinetic misalignment, showing that a multicomponent dark sector comprising the inert scalar and the Majoron can be realized in the model. The resulting framework provides a unified origin for low-scale baryogenesis, neutrino masses, and multicomponent dark sector, so it can be tested by complementary experimental probes through direct detection experiments, collider searches for inert scalars, and future detection of Majoron dark matter or dark radiation.

hep-ph.title: LZ-Motivated Pseudo-Dirac Higgsinos in the Supersymmetric 331 Model from the Supersymmetric \texorpdfstring{$SU(6)$}{SU(6)} GUT Model
hep-ph.author: Imtiaz Khan, Ali Muhammad, G. Mustafa, Farruh Atamurotov, Ahmadjon Abdujabbarov, Mussawir Khan
hep-ph.abstract: The high-recoil event reported by LUX--ZEPLIN motivates a neutral electroweak state with an inelastic splitting in the sub-MeV range. We propose supersymmetric 331 model from the supersymmetric $SU(6)$ GUT model, and we study the electroweakino sector relevant to this recoil. Above the $331$-breaking scale hypercharge is not an independent gauge factor, and the leading bino--wino cancellation is replaced by a relation between the physical $U(1)_X$ and $SU(3)_L$ gaugino invariants, $I_X=-I_L$. A singlet--adjoint gauge-kinetic source also correlates the colored invariant. We diagonalize the neutral gauge--Higgs fermion sector of the renormalizable model and determine the tree-level Higgsino splitting without introducing an effective bino mass by hand. The required solutions form a continuous locus in the gaugino and $331$-breaking parameters. At the reference point, the solution lies close to the leading sum rule, while variation of the $331$-breaking coupling moves the locus continuously. The same calculation tests the ordering of the additional neutral states, the gauge/gaugino contribution to the $331$-breaking scalar mass, and the gravitino ordering. We compare this construction with recent $SU(5)$, singlino-assisted, electroweak-multiplet, nuclear-response and solar-capture analyses of the LZ event.

hep-ph.title: Resonantly-Enhanced Baryogenesis through Asymmetric Capture by Primordial Black Holes
hep-ph.author: Fayez Abu-Ajamieh, Xiaoyan Huo
hep-ph.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) can generate the Baryon Asymmetry of the Universe (BAU) through asymmetric capture of baryon-charge-carrying particles, but previous realizations of this mechanism typically yield an asymmetry well below the observed value because the relevant CP-violating scattering asymmetry is loop suppressed. We show that this limitation can be overcome through resonant CP violation in a mixed system of two nearly degenerate unstable fermions, $Y_{1,2}$, whose mass splitting is comparable to their decay widths. Rare production of the coherent $Y_1$--$Y_2$ state, followed by CP-asymmetric return and loss decays, generates an $\mathcal{O}(0.1)$ difference in integrated decay probabilities while preserving the global baryon charge at the Lagrangian level. Embedding this resonant source in the PBH-capture transport system yields the observed baryon asymmetry. We first reproduce the mechanism in a zero-temperature, sudden-evaporation treatment, which gives $\eta_B^{T=0}\simeq1.74\times10^{-10} \simeq2.00\eta_B^{\rm obs}$. We find that after including thermal corrections and continuous PBH evaporation and entropy production, the resulting BAU becomes $\eta_B = 8.72\times 10^{-11}$ in agreement with the observed value. An interesting finding of the model is that even if PBH absorption remains active, we would still have BAU $\eta_{B}^{\text{no evap}} \sim 9.1 \times 10^{-12} \sim 0.105 \eta_B^{\rm obs}$. We further investigate gravitational-wave signatures associated with the primordial fluctuations responsible for PBH formation. The corresponding scalar-induced gravitational-wave spectra peak at $f \sim 0.16\text{--}0.17~\mathrm{MHz}$, with $h^2\Omega_{\rm GW}^{\rm peak} \sim (3\text{--}7)\times 10^{-8}$. Under idealized sensitivity assumptions, U-DECIGO can achieve signal-to-noise ratios above 10 for the benchmark spectra.

hep-ph.title: A consistent neutrino determination of the low-energy weak mixing angle
hep-ph.author: M. Atzori Corona, M. Cadeddu, N. Cargioli, F. Dordei, L. Ferro, C. Giunti, R. Pavarani, M. Sestu
hep-ph.abstract:
The weak mixing angle, $\sin^2	heta_W$, is a fundamental parameter of the Standard Model and a sensitive probe of electroweak physics across various energy scales. At low momentum transfer, the Standard Model prediction approaches a well-defined low-energy plateau, providing a target for precision tests of the electroweak theory. At the lowest momentum transfer, atomic parity violation (APV) in cesium provides one of the most precise determinations of the weak mixing angle. Here, we review and update the status of this determination and compare it with other available probes. We then consistently reanalyze low-energy neutrino scattering data and combine the resulting determinations from coherent elastic scattering (CE$
u$NS) and neutrino-electron scattering. The complementary sensitivity of these processes to electroweak couplings enables a neutrino-based determination of the low-energy weak mixing angle, accounting for electroweak radiative corrections and relevant theoretical uncertainties. Our global analysis yields $\sin^2	heta_W^{m low}(
u\,	ext{data}) = 0.232\pm 0.006$. We assess the consistency and relative impact of the individual neutrino measurements and discuss the prospects for future CE$
u$NS and neutrino-electron scattering experiments to improve the precision of this determination. Our analysis provides an independent test of the Standard Model at low momentum transfer, complementary to that provided by atomic parity violation.

hep-ph.title: $P$-wave quarkonia in jets at the LHC
hep-ph.author: Taewook Ha, Byungsik Hong, Daekyoung Kang, Soohwan Lee, Bayu Adi Nugraha Putra
hep-ph.abstract: We present the first systematic theoretical study of the production of $P$-wave charmonium states $\chi_{cJ}$ and bottomonium states $\chi_{bJ}(nP)$ within jets at the LHC using the fragmenting jet function framework at next-to-leading order in $\alpha_s$. Our calculation resums both collinear DGLAP logarithms and threshold double logarithms in the fragmentation functions and accounts for feeddown contributions from higher quarkonium states. We observe a notable contrast between the charmonium and bottomonium sectors. For $\chi_{bJ}(nP)$, the normalized momentum-fraction distributions exhibit a nearly universal shape, with remarkably weak dependence on the choice of long-distance matrix element sets, the radial excitation ($n=1,2,3$), and the total angular momentum ($J=0,1,2$). We attribute this universality to the overwhelming dominance of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ fragmentation channel, while feeddown contributions from higher bottomonium states remain small. In contrast, the shape of $\chi_{cJ}$ distributions exhibits a stronger dependence on the matrix-element set, reflecting the different relative contributions of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ and ${}^3P_J^{[1]}$ channels. We provide predictions for the $\chi_{cJ}$ and $\chi_{bJ}(nP)$ distributions for the CMS and LHCb kinematic selections across a range of jet transverse momenta. We also compare our predictions with \textsc{Pythia}~8 simulations for selected $P$-wave quarkonium states.

hep-ph.title: Machine-learning discovery potential for a heavy Higgs boson in $e^+e^-\to ZH$ at a future lepton collider
hep-ph.author: Majid Hashemi
hep-ph.abstract:
A study of the discovery potential for a CP-even heavy neutral Higgs boson $H$ is presented in the Type-I two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM) at a future $e^+e^-$ collider with $\sqrt{s}=500~\mathrm{GeV}$, focusing on the process $e^+e^-	o ZH$ with $H	o WW$, and with $Z	o\ell\ell$ or $Z	o
u
u$. The final states are four jets plus two leptons ($4j2\ell$) and four jets plus missing transverse momentum ($4j2
u$). Both a Boosted Decision Tree (BDT) and a Deep Neural Network (DNN) were trained on the same inputs. The BDT was found to be substantially faster in training and inference without any loss of performance, and it is therefore the classifier used in the interpretation. Three strategies are compared: a cut-based analysis, a one-dimensional BDT selection trained per mass point, and a two-dimensional (BDT $	imes$ $m_H$) template analysed with a profile likelihood. The 2D template improves the expected discovery significance by a factor of $2.5$--$3.6$ in the $4j2\ell$ channel and by a factor of $5$--$18$ in the $4j2
u$ channel relative to the cut-based analysis, with the largest gains at high $m_H$ where the cut-based mass window loses efficiency. We translate the expected exclusions into $95\%$ CL upper limits on $\sigma 	imes$ BR and discuss the implications for the Type-I 2HDM parameter space.

hep-ph.title: Light Mediators at the Neutrino-Dark Matter Frontier: Coherent Scattering, Precision Constraints, and Complementary Searches
hep-ph.author: Raoul Serao, Mohamed Ouchemhou, Antonio Capolupo, Salvatore Capozziello
hep-ph.abstract: Low-threshold neutrino and dark-matter experiments constrain light mediators through different momentum transfers, targets, and coupling combinations. We examine scalar and vector interactions in coherent neutrino--nucleus scattering, neutrino--electron scattering, and dark-matter direct detection. Three representative interaction models are used to compare recoil spectra and coupling degeneracies. For $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ and $^{131}\mathrm{Xe}$, the nuclear-charge response matrix has a condition number of approximately 115, so two different targets may still leave nearly parallel blind directions. An analytic profile-likelihood calculation shows how spectral overlap and uncertainties in neutrino interactions affect dark-matter discovery sensitivity in the neutrino fog. We discuss the implications of measurements from COHERENT, CONUS+, LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T and specify which theoretical inputs, detector responses, and statistical correlations are needed to combine their constraints.keyword : coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering; light mediators; neutrino--electron scattering; dark matter direct detection; non-standard interactions; solar neutrinos; complementarity

hep-ph.title: Study of enhancing the signal-background separation for the Higgs boson production in association with a single top-quark in $pp$ collisions at the LHC
hep-ph.author: Rustam Azimzade, Alina Dadashova, Igor Boiko, Vladimir Lyubushkin, Nazim Huseynov
hep-ph.abstract: In this paper, a multivariate analysis based approach for enhancing the extraction of the rare Standard Model (SM) process being studied - Higgs boson production in association with a single top quark (tH) - from the prevailing background processes is presented. The analysis was performed using a Monte Carlo generated dataset simulating the outcomes of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). A deep fully connected neural network was developed for signal-background discrimination, incorporating a masking mechanism designed to suppress the contribution of input variables associated with objects that were not reconstructed in a given event. The performance of the masked architecture was evaluated on independent Monte Carlo samples. The results of the proposed methodology are compared with a conventional cut-based approach in terms of the statistical significance of the tH production channel. The developed framework was tested using a simulated dataset corresponding approximately to the combined statistical samples of LHC Runs 1, 2, and 3.

hep-ph.title: Inflation, Cosmic Perturbations and Non-Gaussianities
hep-ph.author: Yi Wang
hep-ph.abstract: We review the theory of inflationary perturbations. Perturbations at both linear and nonlinear orders are reviewed. We also review a variety of inflation models, emphasizing their signatures on cosmic perturbations.

hep-ph.title: Searching for axion-like particles with SPHEREx
hep-ph.author: Marco Regis, Marco Taoso, Jorge Terol Calvo
hep-ph.abstract: We study prospects to detect axion-like particles (ALPs) with the upcoming near-infrared telescope SPHEREx. The signal under investigation is the ALP decay into two photons. Assuming dark matter (DM) to be in the form of ALPs, we analyze the signal from the DM halos of dwarf spheroidal galaxies, the Large Magellanic Cloud and the Milky Way. We find that SPHEREx can significantly improve current limits on the axion-photon coupling in the 0.5-3 eV ALP mass range.

hep-ph.title: Dark Energy Crosses the Line: Quantifying and Testing the Evidence for Phantom Crossing
hep-ph.author: Emre Özülker, Eleonora Di Valentino, William Giarè
hep-ph.abstract: Combinations of the most recent CMB, BAO, and SNeIa datasets, when analyzed using the CPL parametrization, $w(a) = w_0 + (1 - a) w_a$, exclude $\Lambda$CDM at $\gtrsim\!3\sigma$ in favor of a dark energy equation of state (EoS) parameter that crosses the phantom divide. We confirm this behavior and show that it persists when DESI BAO data are replaced by SH0ES $H_0$ measurements, despite the known tension between these probes in the presence of CMB data. In both cases, the constraints favor a transition from an early-time phantom-like phase to a late-time quintessence-like phase, with the crossing occurring at different redshifts depending on the dataset combination. The probability that a phantom divide line (PDL) crossing does not occur within the expansion history is excluded at significance levels ranging \mbox{between $3.1\sigma$\,--\,$5.2\sigma$.} To investigate whether the apparent PDL crossing is a genuine feature preferred by the data or an artifact of the linear form of the CPL parametrization, we isolate the PDL crossing feature by introducing two modified versions of CPL that explicitly forbid it: CPL${}_{>a_\mathrm{c}}$ and CPL${}_{<a_\mathrm{c}}$. These models are physically motivated in that they phenomenologically capture the behavior of thawing and freezing scalar field scenarios. While previous studies have primarily considered thawing quintessence as a non-crossing alternative, we find that a freezing phantom-like model is the only one capable of performing comparably to CPL--and only in a few cases. Nevertheless, across all dataset combinations considered, the standard CPL model consistently provides the best fit, strongly indicating that the data genuinely favor a PDL crossing.

hep-ph.title: Quintessential Inflation in Light of ACT DR6
hep-ph.author: Sayantan Choudhury, Swapnil Kumar Singh, Satish Kumar Sahoo
hep-ph.abstract: We analyze the canonical generalized-exponential quintessential-inflation potential in light of ACT DR6 scalar-tilt constraints and the distinct demands of its post-inflationary and late-time evolution. The potential slow-roll hierarchy is derived through fourth order and checked against a numerical scalar and tensor mode calculation. For a benchmark $n=15$, $\lambda=10^{-9}$ at a reference $60$ remaining e-folds, the numerical spectrum gives $n_s\simeq0.96396$, $r\simeq7.71\times10^{-5}$, and a negative running of running of order $10^{-5}$. The exact Hubble-flow endpoint gives a full inflationary excursion exceeding $M_{\rm Pl}$ even though the ten-e-fold observable interval is much smaller. We characterize a phenomenological radiation-injection family followed through kination, radiation and matter domination, and calculate leading-order gravitational-wave transfer spectra with an integrated radiation-density test. A shallow exponential term permits a calibrated late-time quintessence phase, whose homogeneous equation of state and expansion predictions are evaluated numerically. The result is a quantitative map of the coupled inflation, reheating, gravitational-wave and dark-energy requirements, with the limitations of the assumed transfer and thermal history stated explicitly.

hep-ph.title: Searching for Cosmological Collider in the Planck CMB Data II: collider templates and Modal analysis
hep-ph.author: Petar Suman, Dong-Gang Wang, Wuhyun Sohn, James R. Fergusson, E.P.S. Shellard
hep-ph.abstract: Signatures of massive particles during inflation are highly informative targets for cosmological experiments. With recent progress on both theoretical and observational frontiers, we have reached the point where these novel signals of primordial non-Gaussianities (PNG) can be systematically tested with increasingly precise data. In this paper, we present the results of improved CMB data analysis for cosmological collider signals using Planck CMB data. To set the stage, we first construct a set of simplified but characteristic collider templates which are accurate over a broad range of particle masses, spins and sound speeds. In order to break degeneracies with single-field PNG, we propose an orthogonalization scheme such that the collider templates are uncorrelated with the highly constrained equilateral and orthogonal shapes. On this basis, we deploy the Modal bispectrum estimator for the Planck analysis and perform a systematic scan of parameters to search for the most significant collider signal. The maximum signal-to-noise ratio is found to be $2.35\sigma$ for an orthogonalized massive spin-0 exchange after taking into account the look-elsewhere effect. In addition, we cross-validate the Modal analysis with the CMB-BEST pipeline, which demonstrates the consistency of results across the benchmark examples of collider templates. Given the low signal-to-noise ratio regime we find at the current stage of PNG observations, we believe the orthogonalization procedure provides an optimized strategy for future tests of the cosmological collider signals.

hep-ph.title: Classical and quantum evolution of inflationary fluctuations
hep-ph.author: Guillermo Ballesteros, Jesús Gambín Egea, Alejandro Pérez Rodríguez
hep-ph.abstract: We compare the correlation functions of inflationary perturbations computed either with quantum or classical dynamics. Even if they are enforced to agree at a specific time during inflation, classical and quantum correlations will differ at the end of inflation, provided that interactions are relevant. The difference between the results of the classical and quantum computations is exponentially sensi- tive to the number of e-folds elapsed from the time of agreement.
