hep-th.author: Igor Pikovski
hep-th.abstract: Detecting single gravitons is possible through the extraction of discrete energy quanta from passing gravitational waves. For decades, this was considered hopeless, with estimates suggesting a detector the size of Jupiter. Here, I explain how these earlier estimates relied on the highly inefficient electron ionization process, while the absorption through the full mass quadrupole of a macroscopic system can bring graviton detection within experimental reach. Operating in the LIGO frequency band solves the challenges of graviton sources and noise suppression, allowing gravitons to be extracted from known passing gravitational waves and detection events to be heralded by classical gravitational-wave observations. Combined with the ability to resolve single energy quanta in macroscopic systems, such as in quantum acoustics, this opens a realistic path toward graviton detection. I also discuss the general limitations of particle detection in establishing an underlying quantum theory, illustrated by an energy-nonconserving semiclassical alternative. Nevertheless, the semiclassical alternative is not standard classical wave physics, and extracting $E=\hbar\omega$ from a passing wave constitutes bona fide particle detection. This opens the way not only to the first detection of individual gravitons, but also to experimentally probing linearized quantum gravity and the graviton counting statistics of gravitational waves.

hep-th.title: Primordial non-Gaussianity in warm $k$-inflation with nonminimal derivative coupling
hep-th.author: Xiao-Min Zhang, Zi-Xin Bai, Qing-Ze Shi, Run-Qing Zhao, Peng-Cheng Chu, Yun-Cai Feng
hep-th.abstract: This paper derives the finite-inertia intrinsic thermal bispectrum in potential-free warm $k$-inflation with nonminimal derivative coupling (NMDC). On a fixed Friedmann--Lema\^ıtre--Robertson--Walker geometry, the complete cubic inflaton action determines the nonlinear stochastic source, encompassing temporal, spatial-gradient, and field-dependent kinetic interactions. The retarded solution captures the full momentum-triangle dependence while retaining unequal-time correlations, whereas its equilateral limit yields the intrinsic nonlinearity parameter. The power spectrum is computed with the same response and Gaussian initial state, thereby fixing the statistical normalization. A complementary local freeze-out reduction makes the interaction coefficients and two geometric shape contributions explicit. Comparison along an evolving near-attractor trajectory indicates that unequal-time finite-inertia propagation is crucial for quantitatively predicting the intrinsic bispectrum. The analysis also derives the slow-roll-suppressed nonlinear $\delta N$ conversion, together with the Arnowitt--Deser--Misner constraints and cubic vertices that characterize the direct gravitational effects of NMDC. These results clarify the respective roles of local freeze-out estimates and finite-inertia stochastic evolution in the nonlinear prediction.

hep-th.title: Exact and Near-Exact Inverse Renormalization Group with Constrained Monte Carlo
hep-th.author: Dimitrios Bachtis
hep-th.abstract: We establish conditions for exactness of the inverse renormalization group via constrained Markov processes, a class of Monte Carlo simulations which sample the degrees of freedom within a block on a fine lattice under the constraint that they remain consistent with the corresponding degree of freedom on the coarse lattice according to a forward renormalization group transformation. We show analytically, for an arbitrary transformation, that constrained Markov processes correspond to an exact inversion of the renormalization group at the fixed point action, and to a near-exact inversion in the vicinity of the fixed point. We then optimize renormalization group transformations directly on inversely renormalized configurations to effectively map the action onto itself and ensure computational stability in the generation of configurations for high-dimensional systems. Starting from a set of uncorrelated configurations for the three-dimensional $\phi^{4}$ quantum field theory at lattice volume $V=16^{3}$, we invert the renormalization group with constrained Monte Carlo to construct a set of uncorrelated, near-equilibrium configurations for $V=128^{3}$ and extract two critical exponents of the system. The inversion exhibits no critical slowing down, with dynamic critical exponent $z=0.03(2)$.

hep-th.title: An Orbital Curvature for ISCOs
hep-th.author: Poulami Mukherjee, Chandrasekhar Bhamidipati, Sudipta Mukherji
hep-th.abstract: Building on the fact that circular orbits are the fixed points of the phase portraits arising from the geodesic equations on a black hole spacetime, we develop a general orbital geometry, which captures the stability structure of orbits. The construction uses the orbital energy, angular momentum and angular velocity as state space variables, with response functions encoding how the circular orbits react to changes in the black hole background and in their angular motion. The associated scalar curvature provides a geometric diagnostic of certain distinguished points of the circular orbit family, including, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), where it becomes singular. Across the ISCO, the relevant orbital response functions change sign as the system passes from the stable to the unstable circular orbit branch, and typically vanish at marginal stability. We illustrate the framework for Schwarzschild black holes in asymptotically flat four dimensions, and five dimensional Schwarzschild AdS spacetimes. In the four-dimensional case, the ISCO is associated with a degeneration of the energy response sector, while in the five dimensional AdS case it is detected through the angular response. The AdS example also exhibits a separate curvature singularity at a point which coincides with the minimum temperature of the black hole background. These results show that the orbital response geometry provides a unified geometric framework for characterizing the stability of circular orbits and criticality of ISCOs.

hep-th.title: Monopoles, Scattering and Generalized Symmetries on a Quantum Computer
hep-th.author: Oliver O'Brien, Atsushi Ueda, Etienne Granet, Henrik Dreyer, Frank Verstraete
hep-th.abstract: Quantum computers have advanced to the stage that interesting many-body quantum phenomena can be observed. A striking example is the magnetic monopole paradox, a problem that was only solved recently using the language of generalized symmetries. Here we demonstrate a quantum spin chain analogue of magnetic monopole scattering on Quantinuum System Model H2. We implement a novel protocol for preparing a localized quasiparticle wavepacket on top of the ground state. By combining this protocol with time evolution across a duality defect, we efficiently convert local particles into non-local string-like excitations. We demonstrate this particle-to-string conversion in the transverse-field Ising model and a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase of the cluster model. Our results establish duality defects and generalized symmetries as practical resources for preparing and probing non-local excitations on quantum hardware.

hep-th.title: Galois conjugation, droplet growth, and the differential transcendence of the Ising model in nonzero field
hep-th.author: Ran Luo, Jiahua Tian
hep-th.abstract: The square-lattice Ising model is exactly solvable in zero magnetic field, but the scope of exact solutions at nonzero field remains unresolved. We show that, at every fixed dimensionless field $H=h/(k_BT)\ne 0$, its free energy and magnetization obey no algebraic differential equation in the coupling $K=J/(k_BT)$. This excludes Onsager-type formulas and broad classes of special-function expressions. Previous work left open a countable set of fields with algebraic-integer fugacities. We eliminate these exceptions using Galois conjugation and the large-order growth of droplets of reversed spins. At conjugate fugacities outside the unit circle, nearly square droplets produce coefficient growth incompatible with an algebraic differential equation. We prove that cancellations cannot remove this growth in the full pressure series. The free-energy result also holds for the Lieb lattice and square lattices with equal-length chain decorations and uniform coupling and field. In every dimension $d\ge2$, we additionally resolve fields for which $e^{-2|H|}$ has a real algebraic conjugate greater than one.

hep-th.title: Parity-violating scalar-tensor theory revisited: complete basis up to $d=4$ and Hamiltonian analysis
hep-th.author: Yun-Chuan Zhang, Yu-Min Hu, Xian Gao
hep-th.abstract: We construct complete bases of parity-violating generally covariant scalar-tensor (GST) and spatially covariant gravity (SCG) monomials up to derivative grade $d=4$. Including all derivative partitions, each description contains one $d=3$ and thirteen $d=4$ linearly independent monomials. At the level of Lagrangians, we find six integration-by-parts relations that reduce polynomial-type Lagrangians to combinations of one $d=3$ and seven $d=4$ monomials with general coefficient functions. We derive the correspondence between the two bases, retaining general coefficients and total derivatives, and establish their independence under integrations by parts. Among the seven $d=4$ SCG monomials, five contain neither the lapse velocity nor the time derivative of the extrinsic curvature. For the two remaining monomials, we perform a Hamiltonian constraint analysis with a standard Einstein-Hilbert kinetic term and a lapse-dependent potential. On the regular branches considered, the lapse-velocity term propagates four degrees of freedom (DOFs), while the extrinsic-curvature-velocity term propagates six DOFs, whether present alone or together with the lapse-velocity term. These results provide a complete basis for constructing parity-violating scalar-tensor theories with three DOFs up to $d=4$ within this setting, with the parity-violating Lagrangian spanned by six GST polynomials: one $d=3$ and five $d=4$ polynomials.

hep-th.title: Constrained Hamiltonian Formulation of Kinetic Theory for Relativistic Spin-$1/2$ Particles
hep-th.author: Jie Zhou, Ying Shan Zhao, Yifeng Sun
hep-th.abstract: Describing spin transport away from equilibrium requires a kinetic theory that consistently incorporates spin dynamics and phase space structure. We construct such a collisionless kinetic theory for relativistic spin-$1/2$ particles in external electromagnetic fields using the constrained Hamiltonian formalism. The formulation yields both a covariant kinetic equation and its form in independent physical phase space variables, together with the associated noncanonical Poisson brackets and invariant measure. For massive particles, the interplay between the spin constraints and the electromagnetic field makes the particle velocity generally nonparallel to its kinetic momentum and modifies the momentum and spin evolution. The invariant measure in the reduced phase space obeys an exact Liouville identity even for time-dependent fields. This identity and the equations of motion give local conservation of charge and Boltzmann entropy, as well as balance equations for energy-momentum and total angular momentum. The global equilibrium conditions are consistent with covariant statistical mechanics and the Wigner function approach. The massless construction recovers the standard chiral kinetic equations and phase space measure. This framework provides a consistent Hamiltonian description of spin transport beyond equilibrium.

hep-th.title: Algorithmic Construction of Vector-Valued Modular Forms and Application to an $A_4\times\mathbb{Z}_4$-invariant Model of Leptons
hep-th.author: Q. Bonnefoy, M. Rausch de Traubenberg, V. Saulquin
hep-th.abstract: We present an algorithmic procedure that constructs the Vector-Valued Modular Forms (VVMFs) of finite modular groups, as well as its implementation in a companion code. The usual method consists in building the first few VVMFs, whose tensor products then generate the others. We address the difficulty of systematically finding the minimal set of VVMFs that suffices to produce all higher-weight ones, and we propose a method to identify it that makes use of the Burnside-Brauer theorem. For any given group, whose basic group-theoretic and representation-theoretic description is provided by the user, the code determines the minimal set of VVMFs, explicitly builds it using general results of the theory of such functions, then performs the tensor products that generate any other VVMF. Importantly, it automatically takes into account all caveats that might arise during the study of new groups. Our approach reproduces the known results for the finite modular groups explored in the recent phenomenological literature on modular flavor symmetries, and works for additional groups which we tested. We illustrate our algorithm and the working of our code by studying a model of leptons based on the unexplored finite modular group $A_4\times\mathbb{Z}_4$.

hep-th.title: Inflation, Cosmic Perturbations and Non-Gaussianities
hep-th.author: Yi Wang
hep-th.abstract: We review the theory of inflationary perturbations. Perturbations at both linear and nonlinear orders are reviewed. We also review a variety of inflation models, emphasizing their signatures on cosmic perturbations.

hep-th.title: On sufficient conditions for holographic scattering
hep-th.author: Caroline Lima, Sabrina Pasterski, Chris Waddell
hep-th.abstract: Holography implies scattering in the bulk can be mediated by entanglement on the boundary. The connected wedge theorem (CWT) of May, Penington, and Sorce is a concrete example where bulk scattering implies correlation between certain boundary regions. However the converse does not hold. We investigate a recent proposal of Leutheusser and Liu for a generalization of the CWT with converse. We prove the forward direction: having pairs of CFT ``input'' (and likewise ``output'') regions in a phase with connected entanglement wedge implies that a particular bulk subregion (the intersection of ``input'' and ``output'' entanglement wedges) is non-empty. We then establish a modified version of the proposal which has a converse, and identify counter-examples to the stronger conjecture.

hep-th.title: Modified gravity at large scales on quantum spacetime in the IKKT model
hep-th.author: Harold C. Steinacker
hep-th.abstract: The gravitational dynamics of 3+1 dimensional covariant quantum spacetime in the IKKT or IIB matrix model is studied at one loop, combining the Yang-Mills-type matrix action with the induced Einstein-Hilbert action. This combined action leads to interesting modifications of the gravitational dynamics at long distances, governed by modified Einstein equations including an extra geometrical tensor interpreted as ''mirage matter''. In particular we find extra non-Ricci flat geometric modes with a non-standard dispersion relation, with features reminiscent of dark matter and/or dark energy.

hep-th.title: Euler-Heisenberg actions in higher dimensions
hep-th.author: Terry Hatzis, Sergei M. Kuzenko
hep-th.abstract: Using Schwinger's proper-time formalism, we compute the one-loop effective action in both spinor and scalar quantum electrodynamics in $d=2n>4$ dimensions using algebraic techniques. We derive the closed form expression for the corresponding Euler-Heisenberg Lagrangian, and extract its weak-field approximation in 6, 8 and 10 dimensions in terms of invariants of the electromagnetic field. A subsequent analysis of pair production in $d$ dimensions is given. We also elaborate on conformal actions for the electromagnetic field in $d=2n>4$ dimensions. In the $d=6$ and 8 cases, such actions are generated by DeWitt's coefficients $a_3$ and $a_4$ which, for completeness, are re-computed in this work for spinor QED and scalar QED, respectively.

hep-th.title: Classical and quantum evolution of inflationary fluctuations
hep-th.author: Guillermo Ballesteros, Jesús Gambín Egea, Alejandro Pérez Rodríguez
hep-th.abstract: We compare the correlation functions of inflationary perturbations computed either with quantum or classical dynamics. Even if they are enforced to agree at a specific time during inflation, classical and quantum correlations will differ at the end of inflation, provided that interactions are relevant. The difference between the results of the classical and quantum computations is exponentially sensi- tive to the number of e-folds elapsed from the time of agreement. We illustrate this finding with the tree-level bispectrum of the primordial curvature fluctuation and the one-loop power spectrum of tensor modes. We also show that classical evolution from a finite time does not imply the appearance of poles in the scalar bispectrum.

hep-th.title: Finite-time memory detectors and fully constraining Faddeev-Kulish dressings in QED and gravity
hep-th.author: Brett Oertel
hep-th.abstract: We show that for both QED and perturbative quantum gravity, time dependent Faddeev-Kulish dressings can be fully constrained either by symmetry, or by demanding that they reproduce the correct outgoing classical memory contribution. For gravity, we show that using this dressing to construct finite-time Fock spaces allows us to recover both the first order gravitational memory, as well as higher order Christodoulou contributions from the gravitational field. We explain how these higher order perturbative corrections arise in inclusive in-in calculations.

hep-th.title: Ising anyons in the $SU(2)_2$ Chern--Simons theory
hep-th.author: Artem Belov, Andrey Morozov
hep-th.abstract: Ising anyons and $SU(2)_2$ Chern--Simons theory share the fusion rules and $F$-symbols, and their $R$-symbols agree up to braiding orientation and an overall phase. The quantum-group description, $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at $q = e^{i\pi/4}$, is nevertheless not semisimple: tensor powers of the fundamental representation contain an additional spin-$3/2$ representation and reducible indecomposable representations, all of zero quantum dimension. We construct explicit highest-weight bases for up to four strands, compute the Racah and braiding matrices, and show that for four strands changes of fusion basis and braiding mix the physical sector with an indecomposable summand. We prove that this mixing affects neither the braid-closure invariant nor the plat-closure amplitude for any number of strands, so that each braiding matrix can be replaced by its physical block. The full representation theory thus reproduces the Ising-anyon data for all observables relevant to topological quantum computation.

hep-th.title: Effect of $ξRϕ^2$ non-minimal coupling on gravitational light bending
hep-th.author: Ayan Kumar Naskar, Avijit Sen Majumder, Sourav Bhattacharya
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the bending of massless fields by a massive object in the presence of a curvature-scalar $\sqrt{-g}\xi R \phi^2$ non-minimal coupling up to one loop, using the perturbative quantum gravity computations. It is well known that without such coupling a self interacting scalar field theory cannot be renormalised in the presence of gravity. The massive object is modelled by a massive scalar $\phi$, and it is assumed to be non-relativistic, e.g., a star. We compute the 2-2 scattering of massless scalar and photons off this object via graviton exchanges. Assuming both $\xi$ and the bending angle to be small, we use the eikonal approximation to compute the angle up to ${\cal O}(\xi G^2)$. At tree level $({\cal O}(\xi G))$ we find no bending, and hence the ${\cal O}(\xi G^2)$ result happens to be leading in this case. The non-minimal vertices are qualitatively different from that of the standard minimal ones, e.g. $ \sqrt{G} h_{\mu\nu} T^{\mu\nu}$, as the former contains explicit momenta of the gravitons instead of the scalar, complementing the second. The bending angle is found to behave like $\sim b^{-7}$, where $b$ is the impact parameter. We have emphasised the qualitative differences of our results from that of the well studied minimal case.

hep-th.title: Landau's Leviathans
hep-th.author: Vsevolod Chestnov, Giulio Crisanti, Mathieu Giroux
hep-th.abstract: We present a new method together with a proof-of-concept implementation for determining the Landau singularities of Feynman integrals, read off directly from where the Euler characteristic of the associated integral drops. Working over finite fields makes the requisite elimination tractable for multi-scale integrals at the multi-loop frontier. The algorithm returns the genuine and complete set of singularities, subject to a set of conditions which are practically testable. We apply these methods to classes of Feynman integrals beyond the reach of current methods, including non-planar six-point diagrams at two loops, as well as a fully massive three-loop envelope graph. Several of the newly found singularities, both in $d$- and 4-dimensional external kinematics, are of unexpected complexity when compared to previously known singularities for these examples.

hep-th.title: Dissipative hydrodynamic actions and horizon symmetries in gravity
hep-th.author: Mike Blake, Arpit Das, Richard A. Davison
hep-th.abstract: We give a prescription to compute a dissipative action describing the large-scale thermal stress tensor dynamics of a holographic quantum field theory dual to AdS$_4$ gravity, in the context of the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism. Our prescription is valid to quadratic order in perturbations about the thermal equilibrium state. The hydrodynamical degrees of freedom of this action are realised in gravity as relative diffeomorphisms between the black hole horizon and the two asymptotic boundaries of the Crossley-Glorioso-Liu contour. We explicitly compute the action to first order in derivatives, and confirm it correctly reproduces the known hydrodynamic Green's functions. Our prescription requires a choice of horizon boundary conditions for the metric. We study the horizon symmetries that preserve these, and their relation to conjectured hydrodynamic symmetries responsible for many-body quantum chaos.

hep-th.title: Boundary Completion of Vacuum Persistence Probability
hep-th.author: Yu Zhou, Hai-Qing Zhang
hep-th.abstract: The vacuum persistence probability, encoded in the imaginary part of the in-out effective action, is a basic measure of vacuum instability and particle production. However, its evaluation may appear prescription-dependent: the Bogoliubov prescription and the Green's function prescription can yield different results. This discrepancy reflects the incomplete treatment of the endpoint vacuum states in the conventional Green's function reconstruction of the effective action. We establish a boundary-completed reconstruction that consistently incorporates the bulk Green's function and the endpoint vacuum contributions, thereby determining the structure of the complete in-out effective action. The resulting vacuum persistence probability is uniquely determined and agrees with the Bogoliubov result.

hep-th.title: Entanglement in Presence of Topological Interfaces and Dualities
hep-th.author: Christian Northe, Riccardo Poletti, Paolo Rossi
hep-th.abstract: Entanglement through interfaces has attracted considerable attention in 2d conformal field theory (CFT). However, it is known that field-theoretic predictions based on the existing framework are in general incompatible with numerical results [1-4]. A new framework for entanglement through topological defects was recently proposed in [5]. It provides a general description of entanglement through topological defects and successfully reproduces the numerical results for the Ising model in all tested cases and regimes. The key insight is that the relevant quantum correlations are encoded in twisted states, allowing for the construction of the full reduced density matrix (RDM). In this work we pursue two objectives. First, we provide new examples by studying defects in the free boson CFT. Second, we extend the framework to topological interfaces connecting two, possibly distinct, CFTs. Of particular interest are interfaces relating dual theories. We show that the reduced density matrix for a duality interface is the projection of the vacuum reduced density matrix onto a single symmetry sector, closely paralleling the framework of symmetry resolution. Unlike symmetry resolution, however, the projection is imposed by the physical interface itself, demonstrating that duality interfaces reflect quantum correlations back into the entangling interval. We establish this mechanism for diagonal and non-diagonal rational CFTs as well as the free boson CFT. Relative entropy allows us to quantify the distinguishability of the duality interface RDM from the vacuum RDM.

hep-th.title: BRST quantization of Carroll-Weyl gauged null strings
hep-th.author: Sarthak Duary, Sourav Maji
hep-th.abstract: We study the BRST quantization of the null string after completing its local gauge symmetry by Carroll-Weyl transformations. The resulting worldsheet theory possesses three first-class constraints, $C_1 = P^2$, $C_2 = P \cdot X'$, and $C_3 = P \cdot X$, whose modes realize a Weyl-BMS algebra. The additional Carroll-Weyl constraint qualitatively changes the quantum gauge complex: its scalar $s$-ghost is intrinsically coupled to the BMS $bc$-ghost sector, and the anomaly analysis involves three independent cocycles rather than a single Virasoro-type central charge. Starting from the gauge-fixed action, we derive the complete Faddeev-Popov complex, construct the matter and ghost currents and the BRST charge, and evaluate their equal-time operator products in the flipped, equivalently highest-weight, representation. The matter and ghost anomaly coefficients are $(c_{LL},c_{LS},c_{SS})_{\mathrm{matter}}=(2D,-D,-D)$ and $(c_{LL},c_{LS},c_{SS})_{\mathrm{ghost}}=(-54,6,4)$. Because the corresponding central terms multiply linearly independent ghost bilinears in $Q_B^2$, BRST nilpotency requires the three conditions $D=27$, $D=6$, and $D=4$, respectively. These conditions are mutually incompatible. Consequently, there is no target-space dimension in which the minimal flat Carroll-Weyl matter-plus-ghost complex is anomaly-free in the highest-weight representation. The familiar $D=26$ condition of the ILST null string is recovered only after truncation to the two-constraint BMS subsector, which defines a different quantum gauge complex.

hep-th.title: A geometric resolution limit from vacuum entanglement: Topological Structure and Particle-Wave Asymmetry
hep-th.author: Isbelia Martin
hep-th.abstract: We establish that vacuum entanglement entropy, regulated by weak spacetime curvature, imposes a fundamental lower bound on radial resolution for quantum excitations. From the area law, weak gravity introduces a natural UV regulator via the perturbative Green's function. Geometric projection yields a minimal radial scale $\Delta r_{\min} \propto r_s^2/R$, where $r_s$ is the Schwarzschild radius and $R$ the boundary radius. Consistency with the Compton wavelength defines a global mass scale $m_{\text{geo}} \equiv \hbar R/(c r_s^2)$. Particle masses satisfy $m = \alpha m_{\text{geo}}$, where $\alpha$ encodes vacuum structure. For Earth, $m_{\text{geo}} \approx 2.84 \times 10^{-32}$ kg. We determine $\alpha$ via spectral analysis of curvature-induced mode shifts, implemented in Python with $N=3000$ radial points and $n_{\text{modes}}=1000$. The calculation yields $\alpha(2) \approx 33$, matching the electron benchmark without adjustable parameters, ruling out exponential ansätze in favor of slow power-law growth $\alpha(l) \propto l^{1.27}$. Crucially, this resolution limit endows the quantum vacuum with the properties of a granular refractive medium. This elegantly explains a fundamental particle-wave asymmetry: massive excitations with $\lambda_C \ll \Delta r_{\min}$ propagate in the geometric optics limit, following macroscopic gradients as classical geodesics. Conversely, photons with $\lambda \ll \Delta r_{\min}$ interact directly with the medium's granularity, leading to phase decoherence and anomalous dispersion. This framework reframes mass as a probe of vacuum-imposed resolution limits, yielding distinct, falsifiable predictions for high-energy photon propagation.

hep-th.title: Stochastic dynamics from O(2N) fractional Laplacian vector model and O(N) vector model free energy in finite temperature
hep-th.author: WooCheol Shin, Jun Hyuk Lee, Ji-seong Chae, Jae-Hyuk Oh
hep-th.abstract: We explore O(2N) vector model with fractional Laplacian, $\sqrt{-\nabla^2}$ in $d$-dimension and its Hamiltonian dynamics which is described by a Schrodinger type equation. This equation is a kind of current conservation equation, where one can define a current $j(\phi^a)$ of a probability $P(\phi^a)$, where $\phi^a$ is the O(2N) vector field. Naturally, Gibbs entropy $S=-\int [D\phi^a] P(\phi^a)\log P(\phi^a)$ can be considered to explore the system. We realize that this Gibbs entropy of the O(2N) vector model with fractional Laplacian is matched with free energy of O(N) vector model at finite temperature, $1/\beta$ with a deformation, $\mu$ in $d$-dimension. The precise map between the stochastic fictitious time $t$ and the inverse temperature $\beta$ is $\beta=2t$. Therefore, the temperature dependence of the thermal O(N) vector model can be realized as the dynamics of a time dependent solution satisfying Schrodinger type equation. This free energy is obtained by putting O(N) vector model in $S^1\times \mathbb R_d$, where $S^1$ is thermal circle with its periodicity $\beta$. To get $d$-dimensional theory, we sum up all possible frequencies on the circle(so called Matsubara frequency summation) which gives $d$-dimensional thermal partition function. We note that the nontrivial $t$-dependence appears beyond classical limit. To take into account quantum effects, we solve the Hamiltonian dynamics by keeping $\hbar$ corrections. The spectral deformation is mediated by a parameter $l$ such that $\mu=\beta^{-1}\log l$ and so we call this $l$-deformation. This is related to the initial boundary condition of the Schrodinger equation. We also note that the two theories are not equivalent to each other and we just check their correspondence at the level of one-loop determinant, i.e. zero point function in the note.

hep-th.title: Fate of Bouncing Singularities at Finite $G_N$
hep-th.author: Zohar Komargodski
hep-th.abstract: The gravity approximation to a thermal two-point function can develop a complex-time singularity associated with a trajectory that reaches the black-hole singularity. We show that the corresponding singularity is absent at finite $G_N$. This is done by extending Conformal Field Theory analyticity properties to the second sheet (and to the universal cover). We also put two different upper bounds on the amplitude of the correlator at the would-be singularity, by certain finite partial sums, and by a certain partition function on a manifold with nontrivial topology, where two thermal geometries are glued. We discuss the possible implications for the black hole singularity.

hep-th.title: Monopoles, duality, and energy splitting in Chern-Simons QED$_3$
hep-th.author: Shai M. Chester, Éric Dupuis
hep-th.abstract: We compute the scaling dimensions of monopole operators in QED$_3$ with $N$ 2-component complex fermions and Chern-Simons level $k$ to subleading order in the limit where $k,N$ are large and $k/N$ is fixed, which generalizes previous results for scalar QED$_3$ (sQED$_3$) coupled to $N$ complex scalars. In both cases, at leading large $N$ many monopole operators are degenerate, and we compute their energy splitting. We use these results to check the duality between QED$_3$ with $N=1,k=-3/2$ and sQED$_3$ with $N=1,k=2$, whose $U(1)$ monopole symmetry is enhanced to $SO(3)$. We find the scaling dimensions in each dual theory match to high precision for all charges, the lowest charge spin 1 monopoles are close to 2 as expected for the emergent $SO(3)$ current, and the degenerate second lowest charge monopoles match a prediction from a fuzzy sphere calculation, including the energy splitting. We also find similar evidence for dualities between QED$_3$ with $N=1,k=-(2m+1)/2$ and one scalar coupled to two $U(1)$ gauge fields, which has an effective description as sQED$_3$ with $N=1,k=\frac{m+1}{m}$ and $q_s=mq_f$ for $m>1$. Finally, we also find similar evidence for Son's duality between QED$_3$ with $N=1,k=0$ and a free fermion, and clarify a previously discussed match between sQED$_3$ with $N=k=1$ dual to a free fermion.

hep-th.title: Random wave chaos on momentum-fractionated microstate geometries
hep-th.author: Vladan Djukić, Mihailo Čubrović
hep-th.abstract: We study the role of momentum fractionation in the development of chaos on smooth 3-charge supergravity solutions of D1-D5 theory, specifically momentum-fractionated superstrata. We probe the chaos through the dynamics of null geodesics and waves. On fractionated backgrounds, both geodesics and waves show uniformly strong chaos (large chaotic sea and near-perfect agreement with the Berry random wave hypothesis). In contrast, geodesics and waves on single-mode (non-fractionated) superstrata are closer to separability (although still chaotic). We discuss a possibility that such dichotomy can be related to the expectation that monotone BPS states are less chaotic than fortuitous ones. Finally, we explain why our chaos probes are meaningful for microstate geometries even though they become trivial in the black hole limit.

hep-th.title: Non-Coulomb $Q$-cohomology and quantum lifting
hep-th.author: Tanay Kibe, Sam van Leuven, Kayleigh Mathieson
hep-th.abstract: We study quantum lifting of classical $Q$-cohomology classes in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang--Mills theory. Certain powers of the gaugino bilinear $\mathcal{S}=\text{Tr}(\lambda_+\lambda_-)$ in orthogonal theories provide non-Coulomb monotones: multi-graviton classes that vanish upon Cartan restriction. For $SO(7)$, we identify $\mathcal S^4$ as a superconformal descendant of a known lifted monotone class, explaining the latter's non-Coulomb character. We explicitly construct a fortuitous lifting partner for $\mathcal S^4$ that is, by contrast, visible on the Coulomb branch. This construction provides a strategy for finding analogous partners for higher powers at higher ranks. Our main result establishes restrictions on quantum lifting in the multi-trace sector of the classical gauge-group families. We show that the one-loop correction $Q_1$ to the supercharge annihilates every monotone class in classical cohomology, while every $[Q_1]$ image has vanishing Cartan restriction. Thus every non-zero one-loop pairing has a fortuitous source and a non-Coulomb target, and Coulomb monotones survive at this order at finite rank. In the BMN sector, our results imply that non-Coulomb monotones also survive at one loop. A crucial step shows that dressing any classical class by a sufficiently high power of a scalar discriminant yields a multi-graviton class, or zero in cohomology when the original class is non-Coulomb. We interpret this annihilation as a partial no-hair property.

hep-th.title: One-loop unifying relations between Yang-Mills theory and the nonlinear sigma model from Berends-Giele currents
hep-th.author: Zhenhua Guo, Xin Yan
hep-th.abstract: We study unifying relations between Yang-Mills theory and the nonlinear sigma model. We extend tree-level amplitude relations expressed through differential operators to off-shell multiparticle currents and obtain one-loop integrand relations by sewing two off-shell legs. This off-shell approach may also apply to higher-loop integrands.

hep-th.title: Can componentwise D7-tadpole cancellation yield a chiral Standard Model? A no-go for smooth O7$^{-}$ orientifolds
hep-th.author: Mudit Jain
hep-th.abstract: We study a componentwise prescription for D7-tadpole cancellation that includes, as a special case, the local cancellation used in several moduli-stabilisation constructions. We first consider smooth Type IIB Calabi--Yau orientifolds with O7$^{-}$ components of pairwise distinct divisor classes. For each component class $[R_i]$, eight covering-space D7-branes are distributed among smooth irreducible representatives of that class in an orientifold-compatible way. Each component sector may therefore contain several orthogonal, unitary, or symplectic parent factors. We show that these configurations cannot supply the chiral Standard Model through their perturbative D7 spectrum. Without symplectic factors, the entire parent algebra of each component sector embeds into $\mathfrak{so}(8)$ and cannot contain commuting color and weak-isospin subalgebras. Disjointness excludes massless fermions connecting different component sectors, so quark-doublet fermions are absent. Configurations containing symplectic factors require a separate argument: massless hypercharge, together with the same disjointness, forces the net quark-doublet chirality to vanish. Both arguments allow admissible D7 gauge backgrounds and diagonal gauge embeddings, with no restriction on $h^{1,1}_{-}(X)$. We then allow repeated O7 classes, whose D7 sectors can have larger parent groups but necessarily have zero net chirality for both Abelian and non-Abelian gauge backgrounds. We also extend the obstruction to mixed allocations with Whitney remainders supporting no continuous gauge group. We give a geometric condition under which the tadpole forces purely local cancellation. For a specified finite set of allowed D7 support classes, a separate test identifies component sectors in which the tadpole forces componentwise cancellation. We discuss applications to toric constructions and axion potentials.

hep-th.title: Spectral flow in AdS$\mathbf{_3}$ revisited
hep-th.author: Nathan McStay, Ronald Reid-Edwards, Sean Seet
hep-th.abstract: We revisit an old idea that spectral flow in WZW models can be associated with certain $G$-bundles over a worldsheet. This allows us to introduce a novel method for computing correlators of spectrally-flowed vertex operators in WZW models with group $G$ and level $k$, by systematically computing the contribution from a network of line defects. Specialising to the case of $G=SL(2, \mathbb{R})$, as is relevant to AdS$_3$ string theory, we demonstrate that generic $n$-point functions of spectrally-flowed vertex operators at tree level can be rewritten in terms of an $(n+1)$-point function of $n$ unflowed vertex operators and one degenerate insertion. This is to be interpreted as an unflowed $n$-point function in an instanton background. Moreover, we conjecture that this $(n+1)$-point function can be recast as an $n$-point function of unflowed operators and we provide evidence for this. We demonstrate that the $(n+1)$-point function satisfies the same constraints from global spacetime conformal invariance as does an unflowed $n$-point function for a specific choice of spacetime coordinates that we determine. We verify that our results agree with bootstrap results in the literature. This provides the next step towards fully solving the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ WZW model.

hep-th.title: Principles of Quantum Communication Theory: A Modern Approach
hep-th.author: Sumeet Khatri, Ludovico Lami, Mark M. Wilde
hep-th.abstract: This is a preliminary version of a book in progress on the theory of quantum communication. We adopt an information-theoretic perspective throughout and give a comprehensive account of fundamental results in quantum communication theory from the past decade (and earlier), with an emphasis on the modern one-shot-to-asymptotic approach that underlies much of today's state-of-the-art research in this field. In Part I, we cover mathematical preliminaries and provide a detailed study of quantum mechanics from an information-theoretic perspective. We also provide an extensive and thorough review of quantum entropies, and we devote an entire chapter to the study of entanglement measures. Equipped with these essential tools, in Part II we study classical communication (with and without entanglement assistance), entanglement distillation, quantum communication, secret key distillation, and private communication. In Part III, we cover the latest developments in feedback-assisted communication tasks, such as quantum and classical feedback-assisted communication, LOCC-assisted quantum communication, and secret key agreement.

hep-th.title: Are magnetic fields in cosmic voids primordial?
hep-th.author: Deepen Lark, Ruth Durrer, Jennifer Schober
hep-th.abstract: The existence and origin of magnetic fields in cosmic voids remains an open question: Observational evidence inferred from gamma-ray spectra of TeV blazars has been debated for over a decade, while early-Universe magnetogenesis models typically invoke physics beyond the Standard Model of particle physics. We propose a late-Universe contribution to void fields from the dipole components of galactic magnetic fields. In the conducting intergalactic medium, these fields spread through turbulent magnetic diffusion, and the galaxies residing within voids reduce the required propagation distance to a few Mpc, a scale bracketed by current estimates of the turbulent diffusivity. In the regime where the propagation distance is sufficient, the superposition of randomly oriented galactic dipoles produces volume-filling void fields with a white-noise spectrum and amplitudes well above the lower bounds inferred from the absence of GeV halos around TeV blazars. These fields constitute an astrophysical background that must be accounted for before void fields are interpreted as relics of primordial magnetogenesis, and they could account for the void fields without requiring primordial fields at all. Their white-noise spectrum provides a distinctive observational signature.

hep-th.title: Quintessential Inflation in Light of ACT DR6
hep-th.author: Sayantan Choudhury, Swapnil Kumar Singh, Satish Kumar Sahoo
hep-th.abstract: We analyze the canonical generalized-exponential quintessential-inflation potential in light of ACT DR6 scalar-tilt constraints and the distinct demands of its post-inflationary and late-time evolution. The potential slow-roll hierarchy is derived through fourth order and checked against a numerical scalar and tensor mode calculation. For a benchmark $n=15$, $\lambda=10^{-9}$ at a reference $60$ remaining e-folds, the numerical spectrum gives $n_s\simeq0.96396$, $r\simeq7.71\times10^{-5}$, and a negative running of running of order $10^{-5}$. The exact Hubble-flow endpoint gives a full inflationary excursion exceeding $M_{\rm Pl}$ even though the ten-e-fold observable interval is much smaller. We characterize a phenomenological radiation-injection family followed through kination, radiation and matter domination, and calculate leading-order gravitational-wave transfer spectra with an integrated radiation-density test. A shallow exponential term permits a calibrated late-time quintessence phase, whose homogeneous equation of state and expansion predictions are evaluated numerically. The result is a quantitative map of the coupled inflation, reheating, gravitational-wave and dark-energy requirements, with the limitations of the assumed transfer and thermal history stated explicitly.

hep-th.title: Searching for Cosmological Collider in the Planck CMB Data II: collider templates and Modal analysis
hep-th.author: Petar Suman, Dong-Gang Wang, Wuhyun Sohn, James R. Fergusson, E.P.S. Shellard
hep-th.abstract: Signatures of massive particles during inflation are highly informative targets for cosmological experiments. With recent progress on both theoretical and observational frontiers, we have reached the point where these novel signals of primordial non-Gaussianities (PNG) can be systematically tested with increasingly precise data. In this paper, we present the results of improved CMB data analysis for cosmological collider signals using Planck CMB data. To set the stage, we first construct a set of simplified but characteristic collider templates which are accurate over a broad range of particle masses, spins and sound speeds. In order to break degeneracies with single-field PNG, we propose an orthogonalization scheme such that the collider templates are uncorrelated with the highly constrained equilateral and orthogonal shapes. On this basis, we deploy the Modal bispectrum estimator for the Planck analysis and perform a systematic scan of parameters to search for the most significant collider signal. The maximum signal-to-noise ratio is found to be $2.35\sigma$ for an orthogonalized massive spin-0 exchange after taking into account the look-elsewhere effect. In addition, we cross-validate the Modal analysis with the CMB-BEST pipeline, which demonstrates the consistency of results across the benchmark examples of collider templates. Given the low signal-to-noise ratio regime we find at the current stage of PNG observations, we believe the orthogonalization procedure provides an optimized strategy for future tests of the cosmological collider signals.

hep-th.title: Detection of Gravitational Anomaly at Low Acceleration from a Highest-quality Sample of 36 Wide Binaries with Accurate 3D Velocities
hep-th.author: K.-H. Chae, B.-C. Lee, X. Hernandez, V. G. Orlov, D. Lim, D. A. Turnshek, Y.-W. Lee
hep-th.abstract: We set out to accurately measure gravity in the low-acceleration range $(10^{-11},10^{-9})\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$ from 3D motions of isolated wide binary stars. Gaia DR3 provides precise measurements of the four sky-plane components of the 3D relative displacement and velocity ($\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{v}$) for a system, but not comparably precise line-of-sight (radial) separation and velocity $v_{r}$. Based on our new observations and the public databases/publications, we assemble a sample of 36 nearby (distance $<150$pc) wide binaries in the low-acceleration regime with relatively accurate values of $v_r$. Kinematic contaminants such as undetected stellar companions are well under control using various observational diagnostics such as Gaia's {\tt ruwe} parameter, the color-magnitude diagram, multi-epoch observations of radial velocities, Speckle interferometric follow-up observations, and requiring Hipparcos-Gaia proper motion consistency. For $\Gamma \equiv \log_{10}\sqrt{\gamma}$ with $\gamma \equiv G/G_{\rm N}$ (where $G$ is a parameter generalizing Newton's constant $G_{\rm N}$), we find $\Gamma=0.102_{-0.021}^{+0.028}$ for $<10^{-9.1}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$ ($0.132_{-0.027}^{+0.035}$ for $<10^{-9.5}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$) giving a gravity boost factor of $\gamma=1.60_{-0.14}^{+0.24}$, which rules out Newton. This strong anomaly is dominated by two systems (the pairs of HD 189739, HD 189760, and TYC 259-236-1, TYC 259-906-1) that have 3D relative velocities exceeding their estimated Newtonian escape velocities. Without them, we have $\Gamma=0.042_{-0.024}^{+0.027}$ for $<10^{-9.1}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$, $0.057_{-0.031}^{+0.035}$ for $<10^{-9.5}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$, and $0.085_{-0.045}^{+0.059}$ for $<10^{-10.1}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$. Future radial velocity monitoring and Speckle interferometric imaging for larger samples will be useful to refine the present result.

hep-th.title: Mixed Freeze-In and Freeze-Out Histories and Dark-Sector Decays in a $\mathbb{Z}_4$ Two-Scalar Model
hep-th.author: J. P. Carvalho-Corrêa, B. A. Couto e Silva, B. L. Sánchez-Vega
hep-th.abstract: We study dark matter production in a renormalisable $\mathbb{Z}_4$ Higgs-portal model containing a complex scalar $S_A$ and a real scalar $S_B$, where one or both states remain out of thermal equilibrium with the Standard Model bath. We follow their coupled evolution through conversion, semi-annihilation, and the decay $S_B\to S_A S_A$ when kinematically allowed. We impose theoretical consistency conditions, limits on invisible Higgs decays, and LZ direct-detection bounds, accounting for each component's relic fraction. We check WIMP/FIMP assignments against interaction rates. When both states are stable, we find viable FIMP--FIMP and mixed WIMP--FIMP scenarios. In mixed cases, the WIMP-like state remains constrained by its Higgs-portal interactions, with the surviving points mainly concentrated near the Higgs resonance. The FIMP-like state can, however, provide a substantial fraction of the relic density with a negligible direct-detection signal. For $M_{S_B}>2M_{S_A}$, the decay of the heavier scalar leads to three production histories: SuperWIMP production, injection-assisted freeze-out, and sequential freeze-in. The mechanism depends on parent and daughter production. These decays can increase the abundance of a WIMP after freeze-out or contribute to the final abundance of a FIMP, changing the relation between the daughter's Higgs coupling and its relic density. Since the primary decays produce no Standard Model particles, electromagnetic and hadronic BBN bounds on visible decay products do not apply directly. We find $r_{\rm BBN}\ll1$ throughout the retained sample. To assess effects on structure formation, we use the dark matter fraction produced through decays and an equivalent thermal-WDM mass as approximate diagnostics. Some late-decay configurations are flagged as potentially warm, whereas the sequential freeze-in sample satisfies $m_{\rm WDM}^{\rm eq}\gtrsim1~\mathrm{MeV}$.

hep-th.title: Chiral vortical effect and boundary-induced vortical pumping in finite Weyl systems
hep-th.author: B. Q. Song, Pavan Hosur
hep-th.abstract: The chiral vortical effect (CVE) -- an axial current driven by rotation in chiral matter -- appears in systems ranging from relativistic fluids to Weyl semimetals. We present a quantum treatment of a rotating Weyl fermion in a finite cylinder that reproduces the on-axis current density obtained by Vilenkin in an infinite system, while revealing two new phenomena. First, we find that the cross-sectional averaged current density vanishes in the thermodynamic limit, establishing that the bulk vortical response is purely a magnetization current. Second, for spin-polarized boundary conditions, we uncover a robust family of chiral modes that transport axial charge, $\Delta Q=\chi N^2\Delta\theta/4\pi$, under rotation by angle $\Delta\theta$, where $\chi$ is the Weyl node chirality and $N$ is the number of chiral modes. The pump is independent of temperature, Fermi level, and Weyl velocities, but depends on the UV-sensitive number $N$. These results clarify the quantum structure of the bulk CVE and reveal a boundary-enforced chiral spectral structure underlying vortical response in Weyl systems.

hep-th.title: Planckian dissipation from classical hydrodynamics
hep-th.author: Laura Foini, Jorge Kurchan, Silvia Pappalardi
hep-th.abstract: Hydrodynamics describes the long-time, long-distance dynamics of interacting quantum systems by classical equations, yet at low temperature quantum fluctuations might eventually invalidate this classical picture. Here we ask what it takes for a quantum system to sustain a consistently classical hydrodynamic description. Our starting point is the quantum fluctuation-dissipation theorem which, when read in the time domain, acts as a blurring of the fine details of correlation functions on a Planckian time-scale. We analyse how this blurring interacts with the diffusive large-deviation form of correlators assuming the existence of a hydrodynamic light cone velocity, and show that the interior of the cone splits into a classical region, where correlation and response satisfy the classical fluctuation-dissipation relation, and a quantum region, where they deviate sharply from it. We illustrate the mechanism on three phenomenological hydrodynamic equations - diffusion, telegraph and diffusive-telegraph. Preserving a finite classical region as the temperature is lowered forces the current relaxation rate to be bounded from above by the Planckian rate. This bound connects to bounds on diffusivity, equilibration time and shear viscosity. In this way, a Planckian bound on dissipation emerges not as a quantum constraint on microscopic dynamics, but as the price a system pays to remain describable by classical hydrodynamics down to low temperatures.

hep-th.title: Static Quark-Antiquark Interactions in Rotating SU(3) Gluodynamics
hep-th.author: Heng-Tong Ding, Olaf Kaczmarek, Ran Luo, Hai-Tao Shu
hep-th.abstract: We study static quark--antiquark interactions in rotating SU(3) gluodynamics using quenched lattice simulations at imaginary angular velocity. At zero temperature, we extract the static potential from Wilson loops for quark--antiquark pairs aligned with the rotation axis, for transverse pairs with one source on the rotation axis, and for symmetric transverse pairs across the rotation axis. Within the present accuracy, no significant rotation dependence or anisotropy is observed in the zero-temperature potential. At finite temperature, imaginary rotation suppresses the color-averaged free energies obtained from Polyakov-loop correlators in both longitudinal and transverse geometries. Axial-diagonal comparisons are used to identify a bulk region where open-boundary artifacts are reduced. In this region, the large-distance longitudinal free-energy shift is well described by $\Delta F_z(R_{xy})=A R_{xy}^2+B$. The transverse channels exhibit the same qualitative suppression, while their distance dependence additionally reflects the radial arrangement of the static sources and is compatible with a radial single-source free-energy shift in the bulk region. For the finite-temperature observables studied above $T_c$, the response weakens as the temperature is increased. These results provide lattice evidence for a position- and geometry-dependent response of bare static-source free energies to imaginary rotation in a gluonic medium.

hep-th.title: Massive quantum divergence on the Cauchy horizon of a black hole
hep-th.author: Marc Casals, Lorenzo Pisani, Peter Taylor
hep-th.abstract: We investigate a quantum {\it massive} scalar field in the interior of a charged and spherically-symmetric (Reissner-Nordström) black hole. We examine the behaviour for varying values of the black hole charge, field mass and coupling constant when the field is in two quantum states: Hartle-Hawking (representing a black hole in thermal equilibrium) and Unruh (representing a black hole evaporating via the emission of Hawking radiation). We show that the vacuum polarization (in both states) generically {\it diverges} on the Cauchy horizon, in stark contrast to what happens for massless fields; also, the angular components of the quantum stress-energy tensor generically {\it diverge} on the Cauchy horizon and, in at least one of the two states, they do so more strongly than for massless fields. Furthermore, we calculate the energy fluxes in Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates $\{u,v\}$. We show that these fluxes in both states on the Cauchy horizon do not generically vanish. This implies, in particular, that in regular, Kruskal coordinates $\{U,V\}$ the ingoing flux diverges like $V^{-2}$ on the Cauchy horizon (where $V=0$). This divergence suggests that its backreaction via the semiclassical Einstein equations would yield a strong singularity, as opposed to its weaker, classical counterpart. Interestingly, there are exceptions, in which the energy fluxes in Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates vanish: (i) in the extremal limit (where the black hole is maximally charged); (ii) certain fine-tuned regions of parameter space, where the fluxes change sign.

hep-th.title: On Algebraic Background-Independence
hep-th.author: Luka Vinck, Sebastian De Haro
hep-th.abstract: It has recently been claimed that algebraic methods can be used to give a background-independent description of semiclassical gravity. This paper aims to provide an entry point into recent algebraic approaches to quantum gravity and to analyse and critically assess the conception of background-independence here involved. We discuss an algebraic framework for formulating an algebra of observables along the worldline of an observer in a cosmological setting. By 'gravitationally dressing' the observables to the observer's worldline, the reference to the spacetime background can be set aside at the level of the abstract *-algebra. Thus this *-algebra is taken to be independent of any particular spacetime realisation, with different states on the algebra corresponding to different backgrounds. We compare this algebraic framework to three influential notions of background-independence in the literature and argue that none of these fully captures the sense in which the *-algebra is taken to be background-independent. Building on this, we extract a novel notion of algebraic background-independence tied to the representation-independence of the *-algebra. This algebraic conception motivates two further concepts of background-independence tailored to semiclassical theories: semiclassical background-independence and perturbative background-independence. We suggest that these provide useful tools for evaluating the scope and limitations of semiclassical approaches to quantum gravity.

hep-th.title: Minimal-length kinematics of coherent light and a proposed two-color vacuum chronoscopy
hep-th.author: Zhi-Wei Wang, Saurya Das, Samuel L. Braunstein
hep-th.abstract: The unification of quantum theory and general relativity suggests the existence of a minimal measurable length, leading to a generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) and an energy-dependent vacuum group velocity. Testing these effects with macroscopic objects typically encounters the ``soccer-ball problem,'' where applying Planck-scale deformations to the total momentum predicts observationally ruled-out velocity deviations. We adopt the prescription, natural in quantum field theory (QFT), in which the GUP modifies single-mode commutators, and verify by explicit calculation that the macroscopic group velocity of a multimode coherent pulse reduces to the single-photon GUP velocity evaluated at the central wavelength, multiplied by the classical Gaussian-beam factor, with no dependence on the total pulse energy. The energy--momentum relation $E=pc$ itself is unmodified; the deformation enters through the velocity--momentum relation and is equivalent to a modified dispersion relation in the wave vector, with a quadratic coefficient that depends on which of the two variables is used. The soccer-ball problem --- which arises only when the GUP is applied to the center-of-mass momentum of a composite system --- is therefore absent for coherent light, and macroscopic petawatt pulses probe the same parameter space as single high-energy photons. Building on this framework, we propose a two-color vacuum chronoscopy experiment using a short-pulse petawatt laser and its high-harmonic generation. By systematically varying the macroscopic beam waist, our setup separates Planck-scale kinematic shifts from classical diffraction delays, establishing a controlled, source-independent terrestrial methodology whose sensitivity we assess against current astrophysical bounds and against the dominant waist-independent systematics that limit it, residual-gas dispersion and the harmonic birth-time offset.
